  • Organizer Rights: Organizers may delay or cancel segments based on weather or course conditions. No refunds for canceled segments.

Weekly Segment Info:

  • Each week, a segment will be announced—typically a single lap at a local MTB trail. A .gpx file and Strava route will be provided.
  • Recommendation: Use a GPS bike computer (e.g., Garmin or Wahoo) for turn-by-turn directions.
  • Timing: Segments open Monday through Sunday at 6:00 PM. Upload to Strava by Sunday 7:00 PM. If Strava does not capture the segment, the ride will not count—no exceptions!

Rules & Scoring:

  • DNF: If you attempt but fail to capture the segment due to mechanical issues or wrong turns, you’ll receive 1 point (considered a completed segment). Notify organizers at info@fatbikechallenge.com and include the Strava link.
  • Pay close attention to segment start and end points—no adjustments for missed turns or early stops.
  • Shortcuts that provide an unfair advantage may result in disqualification or penalties.
  • You may ride the segment multiple times during the week, but only your fastest time counts.
  • Bike Requirements: Fat bikes only—both wheels must be at least 3.7 inches wide. Using a non-fat bike will result in disqualification.
  • Course Integrity: Marking or modifying the course will result in immediate disqualification.
  • This is not a race—it’s an incentive to ride your fat bike in winter! Be courteous to other trail users and follow park rules.

Prizes & Participation:

  • Riders completing all 8 segments will receive a coupon for a free Ice Cream Cake from Cold Stone Creamery, redeemable only at the Rochester Hills location.
  • Entries: All entries are final and non-refundable. Entries are not transferable.
  • Riders may upgrade/downgrade categories by notifying organizers (points do not transfer).
  • All segments are self-supported.
  • Helmets meeting CPSC, ANSI, Snell, or similar standards are mandatory.

Cake Insurance

New for 2026-27: Cake Insurance, which will allow you to still receive a free Cold Stone Ice Cream cake if you miss one segment.  Below is the process:

  1. Complete 7 segments
  2. For each completed segment, locate the designated Cake Insurance QR Code displayed near the segment and follow the online instructions.  Details of the QR location will be given prior to each segment.
  3. Take a photo of your fat bike near the QR Code as proof and post it to your Strava ride.
  4. Submit all required information prior to the segment close date.

 

See the webpage for scoring details and FAQs.
Join our Facebook page for updates.

Back Alley Bikes brings in 2027 with the 15th annual Bike the Blizzard! 

Back Alley Bikes celebrates the end of our yearly fundraising season with Bike the Blizzard, our winter bike festival where we celebrate donors and partners and come together for group rides, activities, and community as we make it through the coldest part of the year!

As a nonprofit Back Alley Bikes relies on the contributions of community partners, sponsoring businesses, and hundreds and hundreds of small donors to keep our doors open, programs running, and to be the community spot the Detroit bike riders rely on! The rest of the year we are busy with our DIY open shop, educational classes, and getting bikes to people in the city, so at the end of February we come together to celebrate everyone who makes it possible for us to do what we do. Click here to learn more of Back Alley Bikes’ story.

The Black Canyon Crusher takes riders through one of Arizona’s most rugged and scenic desert landscapes. Known for its fast, flowing singletrack and technical rocky sections, the trail challenges competitors with steep climbs, thrilling descents, and sweeping views of the Bradshaw Mountains and Sonoran Desert. Riders navigate a mix of cactus-lined paths, dry creek crossings, and exposed ridgelines that test both endurance and technical skill. With its combination of natural beauty and demanding terrain, the race offers a true test of grit and determination while showcasing one of the state’s premier long-distance trails.

Starting in Mayer, AZ at Chauncey Ranch, 70 mile racers will get to warm up a bit on the road before diving into the single track and heading south. The 35 mile race starts at Deep Canyon Ranch in Black Canyon City, AZ once on the trail will race the lower half of the full course. 

Survive the race and be ready to party. The after party kicks off at the Pioneer Living History Museum, the finish line for both races. Enjoy music and food and the company of the other survivors.  

Registration cost includes entry to the museum for the day as well.

When you register, you’re not just signing up for a race or ride; you’re signing up for an experience. Your registration includes a Dope Rider t-shirt, Morning Snacks & Coffee to fuel your start, Ample Parking for easy convenience to the festivities, SAG Support for any on-road assistance, Aid Stop Food and Drink to keep you hydrated and energized, a Post-Ride Meal and Drink to replenish your energy, Post-ride Entertainment to keep the fun going, and a Post-Ride Drawing for a chance to win exciting prizes. Registration also includes as much Kick-a$$ Photography and Video as our crew can manage to get. All images are uploaded to the Homegrown site for free download.

The post-ride meal is a feast! We will have plenty of vegetarian and meat options, soups, chili, sides, fruit, chips, and snacks. Each registered rider will get two trips through the food line and three trips through the beverage line. (Then until we run out once everyone is full and happy) If you’re bringing guests who want to eat too, you can order an extra meal ticket for them too.

Welcome to the second NYC Velo Festive 5 Boro MTB Challenge!  A special thank you to the folks that helped us put this together:

The Team at NYC Velo

Search and State All Road Apparel

Matt Willet

For those riders familiar with NYC Velo's Fire Tower Brevet series the details of the Festive 5 Boro may seem familiar:

  • The goal of the Festive 5 Boro is to encourage folks to get out and ride a bit during what can be some very cold and bleak riding months
  • The 5 Controles (checkpoints) on the route are the following trail systems in each of the 5 Boros:
    • Van Cortlandt Park in the Bronx
    • Highbridge Park in Manhattan
    • Cunningham Park in Queens
    • Shirley Chisolm Park in Brooklyn
    • Wolfe's Pond Park in Staten Island
  • Riders will notice that there are a few additional trail systems on or adjacent to the route (including Inwood Park, Riverdale Park, Kissena Park, Forest Park, Prospect Park, and Deere Park), note that these trails may not officially allow bikes and any riding on these trails should be done while showing deference to all other trail users – bicycles yield to all other trail users - and as always leaving no trace
  • The "Suggested Route" is approximately 130 miles (including some “downtime” on the Staten Island Ferry), Riders are not required to follow the route, only to visit the trails & the 5 Boro Highpoints
  • Riders who plan to participate are required to register here on BikeReg
  • Riders will produce digital proof of successful Controle check-in/route completion, including start and finish at NYC Velo East Village (via a GPS/Strava file and/or Instagram/social media photos of themselves at the Controle by tagging @nycvelo in the post/reel/story) to qualify for the pin(s)
    • More specifically, riders on Strava should email their completed ride file to info@nycvelo.com
    • For those not on Strava, emailing (or tagging on Instagram) photos of the trailheads and the highpoints to info@nycvelo.com will suffice
    • While following the “Suggested Route” is not required, successful route completion involves riding the trails on the course (not just taking a couple photos and hitting the pavement )– THE TRAIL RIDING IS THE BEST PART!!
  • The official ride start is 5:00am Friday November 27, 2026 at NYC Velo East Village though riders may complete their own adventure at anytime between November 27 2026 and 11:59pm February 28 2027
  • This is an unsupported ride – riders are responsible for their own navigation, hydration, nutrition, equipment, and safety - the use of e-bikes, cars, trains, etc are prohibited to complete the route successfully
  • Riders should take appropriate caution riding on open roads, use appropriate lighting & safety gear for low light or night time riding conditions, and use appropriate safety gear at all times (including helmets, reflective apparel, etc)

 

The Suggested Route:

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53084961
 


Registration:

  • Bikereg handles events like this in an odd fashion: riders must choose specific dates for participation.  When registering for this event just pick a possible date for your ride – riders need not worry if they actually complete the ride on a date that doesn't match their registration

The Tiers of Participation:

  1. There's only 1 Tier: finish the entire route in 18 hours or less and you're a big winner!   
    1. Riders must start and end at NYC Velo East Village
    2. Riders must ride in all 5 noted trail systems (and would probably enjoy riding all of the trails on the route, so they should ride those too) and visit the 5 highpoints of each boro
    3. All of the above must be completed in 18 hours or less (elapsed time – Brevet-Style -- from your start at NYC Velo in the East Village to your finish back at NYC Velo — riding time is not relevant here)
    4. Riders are restricted to the use of one (non-electric-powered) bicycle of any kind (MTB, gravel, road bike if you like a challenge, etc)

Rewards:

  1. For successful route completion:
    1. Riders who satisfy the above criteria between 11/27/26 and 2/28/27 will receive a custom red “FESTIVE” and a custom green “5 BORO” enamel pin (see below)

    2. Furthermore, riders who complete the course between 12/20/25 and 1/1/26 will also receive a custom “NYC Velo Explorers Club” patch

    3. As it happens, the Festive 5 Boro route includes navigation to the high points of all 5 boros, successful completion of the route includes a visit to each one of these high points:

      1. Bennett Park in Washington Heights, Manhattan (265.05 feet, 40.85298° N, 73.93824° W), scan the QR code and type you name into the resulting document to record a successful visit to the Bronx highpoint
      2. Villanova Heights in Fieldston, the Bronx (285.63 feet, 40.897494° N, 73.904898° W)

        1. Note that the actual high point in the Bronx is now on private property so we have posted a QR Code at the telephone pole at the Southwest corner of the intersection of Grosvenor Avenue & W 250th St – scan the QR code and type you name into the resulting document to record a successful visit to the Bronx highpoint 

      3. North Shore Towers Country Club in Queens (258.2 feet, 40.758005° N, 73.719715° W)

        1. Note that the actual hight point in Queens is now on private property so we have posted a QR code on the fence on the north side of the westbound lane of the Grand Central Parkway Service Road bordering the Country Club Golf Course (see the photo below) scan the QR code and type you name into the resulting document to record a successful visit to the Queens highpoint

      4. Battle Hill in Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn (216 feet, 40.65776° N, 73.98828° W)
        1. Note that bikes are not permitted in Green-Wood Cemetery so you'll have to leave your bike with the Cemetery gate attendant (or lock it up outside of the Cemetery) and walk to the Battle Hill Monument
      5. Todt Hill in Staten Island (401 feet, the highest point on the Eastern Seaboard between Florida and Maine, 40.600488° N, 74.114788° W)

        1. Note that the actual high point of Staten Island is in a wooded area and not currently marked so we have posted a QR code attached to a tree at the approximate highpoint (see the photo below) - scan the QR code and type you name into the resulting document to record a successful visit to the Staten Island highpoint  

      Enjoy the ride!

VALLEY OF TEARS GRAVEL

 

March 5–6, 2027 | Turkey, Texas

 

Valley of Tears returns to Turkey, Texas, for its fourth year of racing in the Texas Panhandle.

 

What started as a gravel race in a small Texas town has grown into a weekend that brings together some of the biggest names in the sport, competitive amateurs, and riders from across the country.

 

The racing is fast, the terrain is unforgiving, and the experience goes well beyond the finish line.

 

FRIDAY | DIRT CRIT & EXPO

 

The weekend kicks off in downtown Turkey with the Valley of Tears Dirt Crit. Short, fast, and aggressive racing featuring top professional talent, a substantial prize purse, and plenty of action for spectators.

 

Friday also brings the event expo, free Kids Crit, and an evening of racing and hanging out in Turkey.

 

SATURDAY | VALLEY OF TEARS GRAVEL

 

Saturday takes riders into the rugged landscape of the Texas Panhandle and Caprock Canyons State Park.

 

Expect fast gravel roads, challenging climbs, technical sections, and some of the most unique terrain in gravel racing. Whether you’re lining up to compete at the front or taking on your own challenge, Valley of Tears delivers a course and experience you won’t soon forget.

 

And when the racing ends, the weekend isn’t over. The post-race gathering at Hotel Turkey has become a Valley of Tears tradition.

 

THE DETAILS

 

March 5–6, 2027

Turkey, Texas

1,000 rider field limit

Friday Dirt Crit, expo & free Kids Crit

Saturday gravel racing through Caprock Canyons

Post-race celebration at Hotel Turkey

 

Four years in, we’re just getting started.

 

See you in Turkey.

Remember, this is an UNSUPPORTED ride (not a race): there is NO support, NO sag stops, NOR support vehicles. The course will NOT be marked, and there will be NO printouts prior to the ride. YOU are 100% responsible for YOU, YOUR welfare, YOUR equipment, YOUR navigation, and YOUR own food and drink. If you need a juice box and a hug every 20 miles, this is not the ride for you, please stay home.

You MUST have a registration on your smart phone enter the facility - everyone in the car must be registered...no execptions.  

If you show up without a registration, you will be sent to the spot for unruly people...  

Thank you -

EventNotes:
Fifth Annual Belgian Waffle Ride Arizona

March 5–6, 2027 | Sonoran Desert, Arizona

Hell of the North Desert

Welkom to the fifth annual Belgian Waffle Ride Arizona, our early-season appointment with the Sonoran Desert and its rather creative ways of making a bicycle ride difficult and fun at the same time. The Hell of the North Desert, also known as the Disneyland of gravel, returns March 5–6, 2027, bringing the BWR community together for a weekend of Unroad riding, waffles and well-earned celebration at McDowell Mountain Park.

The desert supplies the scenery. The course supplies the whoops, wonder, wallowing, and wickedness. Expect the Arizona character riders have come to know: open gravel, sandy washes, not-too-rocky terrain and twisting trails, with pavement connecting the sectors and giving your hands a brief chance to forgive you. It takes more than a big engine to ride this place well.

Choose the full Waffle, the middle-distance Wafer or the shorter Wanna. Each gives riders a different helping of the same desert experience, with enough changing terrain to keep bike choice, handling and pacing in the conversation.

Weekend experience

The weekend brings together rider check-in, the Unroad Expo, riding and the post-ride gathering. Meet the brands, catch up with your people, eat waffles and leave enough time for the stories afterward. The detailed 2027 program, venue and start times will be announced on the event page.

2026 Course Reference

 

Final 2027 routes and venue will be announced separately.

Series status

The 2027 Quad-Tripel Crown calendar and competition format are still being finalized. Participating events, scoring and the number of results required will be announced separately. Utah will not be part of the Crown series because it will operate as a standalone UCI Gravel World Series qualifier. 

Fifth Annual BWR Arizona Rider Information

Rider perks

The BWR rider offering includes the following. Final category details and partner offers will appear in registration and the Race Bijbel.

  • BWR musette bag from Neversecond with race-day essentials and sponsor swag
  • BWR branded memento or BWR Bucks for use with participating partners
  • Race number and RFID timing tag for the official finishing time
  • Pre- and post-ride waffles, coffee and beverages
  • Stocked feed zones with hydration and nutrition, including Neversecond
  • Marked courses, traffic control at designated locations and on-course support
  • Post-ride beer and the BWR community celebration
  • Finisher’s trophy beer, with the offering determined by distance and event
  • Unroad Expo access and opportunities to meet cycling brands and partners
  • Bragging rights and more than enough material for the next group ride
  • Podium recognition for the top three in each Waffle and Wafer age category and the top five overall, subject to final 2027 category rules

Official BWR t-shirts, apparel and branded gear will be available through registration and the BWR merchandise area at the expo.

BWR sponsors

We are grateful to the partners who help bring the Unroad to life: Neversecond, Capriroso, ALMSTHRE, The Lost Abbey, Athletic Brewing Co., Van Rysel Bikes, Unwaffle, UNDERBUDR, FORMULA 100, Bolt and Birdworx.

EventName: 38th Gator Ride, Gear Up to End Hunger
EventNotes:
Ready to make a difference while enjoying an unforgettable cycling experience? Join us for the 38th Annual Gator Ride, where your pedals have the power to change lives!

This year’s ride takes you on an incredible journey over the iconic Fred Hartman Bridge, offering breathtaking views of the San Jacinto Monument, plus a ride on the historic Lynchburg Ferry. Not quite the route for you? No worries, our 33 and 53 routes offer thrills without quite so many chills.

Whether you're a seasoned cyclist or just looking for a great cause to support, this ride is for you!

But this isn't just about the ride; it's about putting your pedals to the metal and your dollars to good use. Every mile you cover helps us step closer to ending hunger in our community. Your participation and support will provide essential meals and resources for those in need.

As an MS150 Additional Training Ride, bikemstexas150.org, you need to schedule this event. The courses are 33, 43, 53, and 63 miles. There is even a 6-mile family ride!

All proceeds from the Gator Ride, Gear Up to End Hunger, will go toward our Annual Campaign. Food is a basic need for survival, and too many families in our community need food assistance. Hearts and Hands of Baytown is leading the fight to address food insecurity by providing access to fresh, healthy food via our six-pillar programs. In all our endeavors, we work to remove the stigma of needing food and give clients opportunities to work toward self-sufficiency.

With support like yours, we can provide food for families in a dignified, supportive way while expanding services through collaborative partnerships to eradicate hunger and address its underlying causes. All proceeds from the event go directly back into our community.

Our number one priority for all rides is safety. All riders must wear an assigned number bib to prove their registration. We do our best to provide as much help as possible along all routes with First Aid responders, volunteer marshals, SAG drivers, and Rest Stop crews. We can only be responsible for those registered with their assigned bib number. All riders must wear a helmet.

EventName: Women on Wheels Mountain Biking of Georgia Free Clinic and Ride
EventNotes:
Welcome to the Women on Wheels Mountain Biking of Georgia Clinic registration page. We are so glad you decided to Join the Ride! 

Make sure you join us at Facebook page 

All of our Free Clinics are held at Blankets Creek Mountain Bike Trails, 2261 Sixes Road, Canton, GA. 

Please note: Riders must be at least 16 years old to participate in this event.

The clinics are on the first Saturday of every month, year-round. 

November through March, the clinics are from 2 pm to 4 pm. From April to October, the clinics are 10 am to noon.  In event of bad weather or trail closures, WOW will cancel the event 1 hour before the event starts. The cancellation notice will be posted on Facebook and an email from BikeReg will be sent to all registered participants. 

The clinics require you to be registered and the waiver signed. When filling out the registration, please choose the Level that best suits your skill and fitness level. There are Level descriptions below each group to help you choose which group to join. 

If you’re new to mountain biking OR have never done a fundamentals skills clinic we REALLY recommend starting with the Fundamental Skills Clinic. We feel taking this course from one of our certified instructors will help improve your riding skills.  

We’ll have amazing volunteers leading and sweeping the rides to ensure everyone has a fantastic time. 

Can’t wait to ride with you all!
PresentedBy: Women on Wheels Mountain Biking of Georgia

EventName: IditaFAT Fat Bike Race at Winona Forest
EventNotes:
Welcome to IditaFAT 2027!

Join us Saturday, March 6, 2027, at Winona Forest on the Tug Hill Plateau for another edition of IditaFAT!

Experience winter fat biking at its best on Winona Forest's beautiful network of groomed trails. Known for its legendary Tug Hill snowfall and outstanding winter recreation, Winona Forest provides a spectacular setting for a day of riding and racing.

Whether you're joining us for the relaxed 8K Citizens Ride, lining up for the competitive 20K race, or taking on the 40K endurance challenge, there's an IditaFAT experience for everyone.

Choose Your Ride

  • 8K Citizens Ride: A fun, recreational ride for those looking to experience winter fat biking without the pressure of competition.

  • 20K Fat Bike Race: Fast, flowing winter singletrack and a competitive race experience.

  • 40K Fat Bike Endurance Race: A longer-distance challenge that rewards endurance, fitness, and bike-handling skills.

Event Details

Date: Saturday, March 6, 2027

Time: 9am 

Location: Winona Forest, Mannsville, NY

Region: Tug Hill Plateau, Central New York

Come ride, race, and enjoy the winter wonderland of Winona Forest. Whether you're here to compete or simply enjoy the trails, there's a place for you at IditaFAT!

See you at the starting line!  Think snow!

Start off your 2027 season with our 13th anniversary edition of the Road Apple Roubaix.  This gravel road ride will test riders with plenty of gravel, some pavement, potential mud and perhaps even some snow and ice!   This is an opportunity to tour some of the less travelled roads out in Amish country…JUST BEWARE OF THE ROAD APPLES!  For 2027, there are only two route options- 25 & 50 miles.

About The Ride

  • It is a scenic tour through the country road of Portage and Geauga County.
  • Cyclocross, Mountain, Single-Speed, Fixed gear, Fatbikes and tandem bicycles are welcome.  Road bikes will not be well-suited for this course.
  • The course is will be marked prior to the event and maps will be available. Course marshals will NOT be at every corner or intersection, rules of the road apply!
  • The course will NOT be closed to traffic and does not have a rolling escort. Cycling rules of the road apply, i.e. stop at all stop signs, yield to cars, no more than 2 riders abreast and do not cross yellow center line. Please do not litter.
  • A sag vehicle will be on course to help out riders.

All participants will get a free t-shirt, pint glass (t-shirts and glasses limited to first 400 registered), free drink, free chili bowl and timing.

We will have a mass start at 10 AM sharp of the 25 & 50 milers.  Chip timing for finishers will again be available, but this event is ran as a fondo, not a race.  Note, registration will be capped at 500 participants.
PresentedBy: Road Apple Roubaix presented by Eddy Bike Shop

EventName: The Outer Limits SHAM 6HR MTB Challenge
EventNotes:
Planning

Course

The route is 13 miles, 1300 feet of elevation gain per lap on some of the best singletrack on offer!  Download the .gpx below!

Outer Limits SHAM Fondo.gpx

Downloads (off-site links)

Coming soon.

Lodging and camping

There are many hotels and short term rentals in Hot Springs, but book early as March is SPRING BREAK season and things book up fast!

Event day

Parking

Northwoods Water Works Trailhead 300 Pineland Drive, Hot Springs, AR 71901

Packet pickup

Friday 7:30am-2pm at Red Light Roastery, 873 Park Ave in Hot Springs OR Saturday morning at 8am-8:45am just before the start of the event. 

Aid stations

The only SHAM provided aid is at the Start/Finish area that you will pass every 13 mile lap you complete.  We will have water, snacks, heckling and encouragement!

Spectator guidelines

Heckling is ok. Make some noise! Cowbells! MORE Cowbell!

Event rules

Yes, even SHAM has a few rules.

1. Ride your bike.  The same bike the entire day.  You can make repairs along the way including replacing parts, wheels, tires, tubes, anything! BUT the frame is the same for the whole ride. Carry what you need to make repairs on the trail! You can help others with repairs along the way if you want. If you must leave the course to make a repair you must re-enter the course in the same location you left it.

2. The Course: Study the course. Know the course. Load the course GPX on your device if that's your thing. Tape a cue sheet to your top tube.  There will be markings of barricade tape before and after each intersection/hub. It is NOT a closed course, so the marking tape will not block any other trail openings. Follow the tape.  There will be other people hiking, biking, dog-walking, one-wheeling, generally using the trails. BE KIND to all trail users. 

3. Fueling: This is a self supported ride while on the course.  The Start/Finish area will have high-fives, encouragement, coffee, water and snacks available every time you make a lap.  Have a nutrition plan for yourself on the bike.  You don't have to carry 6 hours of nutrition with you as you will pass through the start/finish area every 13(ish) miles. There will be an area for each rider to put extra nutrition to reload bottles, pockets, etc. after each lap. You can also go to your car in the parking lot between laps if needed but that WAY UP THE HILL! Put a bag of goodies at the start/finish area!

Food and beverage at the Water Works Trailhead Start/Finish Portal

Water, Bananas, Tacos, Bubbly Water, BYO-other beverages.

EventAddress: 17520 Elizabeth Lake Rd, Lake Hughes, CA 93532
EventNotes:
Since 2019 L.A. Tourist has been putting on some form of Dirt related events, riders have chosen to use CX bikes, MTB bikes and what has become known as Gravel bikes.  Now L.A. Tourist brings you a Gravel specific event, no question about it this is a Gravel bike event.  Let's Do it! 40 miles and 5k in our local BIG mountains await you.  This is a true gravel event so bring a gravel bike, cx bike or a hardtail mtb for more comfort.  

We will be providing a breakfast at the start, 2 aid stations and a finisher party so no need to over pack like on most L.A. Tourist events .   This is taking place on March 6 so make sure to layer up cuz it could be freezing.   

This race will be happening Rain or Shine, we do not cancel or postpone due to rain or snow.  These events can take you well above 5k of elevation,  You may ride thru snow , depending on the weather so prepare yourself and keep an eye on the weather as event day approaches. 

Like all L.A. Tourist Events This is an analog event, meaning NO E-Bikes

EventName: Langley Speedway Criterium - VACA BAR Event
EventNotes:
On-Line Registration closes Friday, March 5th, at 8PM on BikeReg.com or race day registration 30 minutes prior.

2026 Series Winners must preregister and email me with your category to receive $7.00 entry.

Course: Langley is a fast, .4 mile stock car oval with nice wide corners. This is considered a “flat” track by auto racing standards, but the corners are still banked for your speedy pleasure.

Location: 11 Dale Lemonds Drive, Hampton, VA 23666. Plenty of parking is available right next to the track. If you have a team tent you can set it up in the infield of the track.

Registration: Register online at www.bikereg.com . Online registration closes at 8PM on Friday, March 5th. Day-of registration opens at 7:15 AM and is available for $40. A second race is just $20. Entry fees include $5.99 USAC fee and $1.00 VCA BAR fee. 2025 VCA Series Winners must pre-register and email the promoter their category to receive $7.00 entry. If you are a promoter of a race in the VCA series you are eligible for $7.00 entry and must pre-register and email the promoter with your category.

License: Beginner One-day and Annual licenses will be available for purchase on race day. Experienced riders must renew their annual license or purchase a one-day license online from USA Cycling. Race Licenses from other countries will not be accepted. Please ensure that you have a USA Cycling License.

Rules: All USAC rules apply. ANSI Z90.4 approved helmets are required to be worn whenever riding on or near the race course. No aero bars permitted in mass start races. No Cat 5/Novice riders permitted in Masters races. No refunds. Events held rain or shine, however the race directors and officials reserve the right to cancel the event in the case of severe weather as deemed necessary for safety.

For questions contact Graham Costa at teamhamptonroads@gmail.com or call (757) 660-2117

EventNotes:
Dirty Kitten Winter Training Series 7.0

Hosted by Dirty Kitten Productions

DKWTS is a fun, diy/virtual training challenge that provides motivation, community, and friendly-competition during the winter for anyone and everyone. You can ride ANY bike, ANY where, ANY time! DKWTS is not a super-serious, competitive, training program for fancy, professional riders. 

OVERVIEW: This year's series will be different in some ways and similar in others. DKWTS 2027 will run for 9 weeks starting on January 4th and ending on March 7th with an optional Prologue period available the week before (December 28th - January 3rd) as well as an IRL “DKWTS Finale Ride” in Frederick, MD in early March (details TBA).

There will be daily, weekly, and monthly challenges; virtual group rides; live streams, activities, and group chats; friendly competitions; prizes; giveaways; and other general shenanigans!

DATES: January 4 - March 7, 2027

REGISTRATION: December 1, 2026 - January 31, 2027

www.BikeReg.com/dirty-kitten-winter-training-series

ENTRY: Starting at $40 on December 1st - Early Kitten Pricing!

Registration increases on 12/7 ($45), 12/14 ($50), 12/21 ($55), 12/28 ($60), 1/4 ($65)*

*Party Purritos (non-competitive) receive a $5 discount; Junior riders (under 18) receive a $10 discount

REFERRALS: After registration, you will receive a unique referral code to share with friends, family, teammates, strangers. If 5 people register using your code, you will receive a FREE winter training series entry for a friend. Share it as many times as you like and win multiple free entries to giveaway!

TEAMS: Enter a team, club, or group name when you register and receive 1 FREE entry to giveaway for every 5 members who join the series! (All member must register with the same team/club/group name)

CATEGORIES & FIELDS: Categories will be fluid and may change based on participation, performance, etc throughout the series. Some examples of possible category and field groupings are...

  • Gender - Women, Non-Binary, Men
  • Age (ex. Under 18, 25-29, 33-37, 40+, 55+, 63-69, 75.5+)
  • Metrics - Time, Distance, Elevation (ex. weekly average)
  • Party Purritos - Just doin' it for the shenanigans!

*Separate categories & fields will be created on the DKWTS challenge leaderboard (TBA)

DKWTS CHALLENGES: DKWTS consists of various challenges that allow participants to gain points (Purrito Points!) throughout the series: Tours (main challenges that last multiple weeks), Stages (smaller challenges that last up to 1 week), and Bonuses (random challenges that last different lengths of time).

  • TOUR CHALLENGES: Tour Challenges are based on a rider’s progress for time, distance, and elevation metrics over a multi-week period. Purrito Points will be assigned for rider participation each Tour.
  • STAGE CHALLENGES: Stage Challenges are weekly challenges that give riders the opportunity to earn points. Some stages may be "competitive" (i.e. Longest ride of the week) with points awarded to the Top riders in each designated category and field. Other stages are "participatory" (i.e. Do a ride on 5 different days this week) with points awarded to all who complete the challenge. NOTE: Some of the challenges may have separate scoring for virtual and outdoor rides.
  • BONUS & POP-UP CHALLENGES: Bonus & Pop-Up Challenges are announced throughout the competition as fun ways for riders to earn additional points and interact with other participants. Bonus Challenges are usually announced at the beginning of each week or Stage. Pop-Up Challenges are surprise challenges announced randomly throughout the series. Some examples of Bonus & Pop-Up Challenges are: Zwift Meet-Up Rides, Real Life/Outdoor Rides, Segment Challenges, Social Media Challenges, Cross-Training Activities, Photo Challenges.  

TEAM CHALLENGE: Throughout the series, we will give various shout-outs to the team/club/group with the most members registered; most participation; highest point total; etc. Team challenges are mostly for bragging rights.

SCORING: The points breakdown is TBA and will be available on the DKWTS website. Participants will receive points for various challenges and activities such as…

  • Time, Distance, Elevation Challenges
  • Overall Stage & Tour Challenges
  • Bonus & Pop-Up Activities
  • Overall Team Points

VIRTUAL GROUP RIDES: DK Zwift Club

*Rides are subject to change - full details will be shared closer to the series start date. Ride chat available on Discord.

  • Monday Night Recovery Ride (PM)

  • Tuesday Night Zoomies (PM)

  • Wednesday Workout (AM/PM)

  • Thursday Early Bird Ride (AM)

  • Thursday Evening Climbing Ride (PM)

  • Friday Morning Coffee & Trivia (AM)

PRIZES & GIVEAWAYS: TBA (provided by our beloved and generous event sponsors & partners)

Various prizes & giveaways will be awarded during the series based on Purrito Points and at random. Prizes may include Dirty Kitten merchandise items, sponsor giveaways, partner event entries, and more!

RULES & OTHER IMPORTANT THINGS YOU NEED TO KNOW:

#1. Have Fun, Be Safe, Don’t be a Jerk!

#2. This is designed to be a FUN & friendly winter training challenge (i.e. friendly competition).

#3. Any 2-wheeled, non-motorized bicycle may be used (pedal assist e-bikes are allowed but scoring may be adjusted to compensate for various advantages).

#4. All participants are required to sign an online waiver through BikeReg when registering for the event.

#5. Participants must sign-in to and use our custom DKWTS leaderboard application to participate (see our Privacy Policy below). If you participated in DKWTS last year, log in using your existing account - you DO NOT have to create a new one.

#6. Participants must authorize the Dirty Kitten Winter Training Series (DKWTS) leaderboard app to load or sync their ride data either manually, from Strava, or from another device - read our Strava API Usage Policy below.

#7. Rides should be uploaded and made visible (not private) within 24-hours of the end of the ride. Exceptions will be made for extenuating circumstances.

#8. NO duplicated ride data (i.e. uploading the same ride twice from both Zwift & Garmin).

#9. Categories & fields will be determined by the Event Directors (Chris, Alex, and Snowy) based on registration, participation, and challenge data. They may change throughout the series without warning or explanation.

#10. We ask that you limit your personal support emails to ONE inquiry a week (unless you are registered as a “High Maintenance" Purrito). If you are sending us multiple request emails, we may start deducting points based on the amount of time needed to address your issue ESPECIALLY if it's something that has been previously addressed (rude & disrespectful emails, messages, comments will result in greater point deductions so please be nice - see Rule #1). That means: Read the Event Notes, emails, website, and updates; review the weekly Live Streams; visit our social pages; ask your friends, or use any of the other resources provided. We love you ALL but can't respond to 400+ emails a day (Snowy gets overwhelmed and needs a break). Please give us 48-hours to respond to your inquiry or request.

#11. Event Directors reserve the right to penalize or disqualify anyone for cheating or displaying inappropriate conduct towards other participants in the series. Dirty Kitten is dedicated to providing fun, safe, and inclusive events for ALL participants. We will NOT tolerate any hateful, disrespectful, or inappropriate language/actions at our events. 

#12. A 48-hour “protest period” will follow any leaderboard updates. You may contact us with questions or concerns about your points or scores during that time. After 48-hours, the “protest” window will close and all scores will be finalized. Be sure you keep paws on your Purrito Points!

#13. Additional Bonus Purrito Points may be awarded throughout the series at the Event Directors' discretion.

#14. Various prizes and giveaways will be awarded and announced throughout the series.

#15. Sorry, no registration refunds or transfers. All registration is final.

Participation in this virtual series is AT YOUR OWN RISK. By signing the online waiver, participants agree to follow the appropriate “rules of the road” (or trail) wherever they ride, as well as adhere to proper state/regional/municipal bike usage and safety guidelines. Dirty Kitten Productions, Dirty Kitten Gravel, Dirty Kitten Racing, the Event Directors, BikeReg, Strava, Zwift, Garmin, Wahoo, and all event partners/sponsors are released of any liability during the entirety of the series.

DK GROUPS & CLUBS: Information and updates will be sent out each week via email, as well as posted on the Dirty Kitten Gravel and Dirty Kitten Productions social media pages (FB & IG). To stay involved, join our Ride Dirty Community Group on FB and our Dirty Kitten Discord. If you are on Strava, join our Dirty Kitten Gravel Strava Club. If you are on Zwift, join our Dirty Kitten Gravel Zwift Club. Subscribe to our Dirty Kitten YouTube Channel for weekly live updates and DKWTS Q&A sessions.

DK SCHOLARSHIP FUN: Please consider contributing to our "DK Scholarship Fund" and help make our events accessible to everyone (see info on our merchandise page when registering).

What’s this all about?

YES. YOU CAN CHANGE YOUR CLASS TO FATBIKE ANYTIME EVEN DAY OF

 To encourage more participation and in an effort to have more inclusion to this shit show on wheels. We've reduced the registration fee for women to $20. Please spread the word.

Winterräden is German for winter bike.
We’re pretty sure.
Google said so.

This is a bike race that is anything but regular. First off, it’s in February. In New England. It’s run by the Urban Assault Build Crew  link to  DirtwireTV, which means pretty much anything can—and probably will—happen.

Weather will absolutely dictate how this event runs. Start times, course length, and categories may change on race day, because we are not wizards and definitely not Nostradamus.

This is an 18+ event.
Food vendors, Industry Vendors, beer garden, and other adult beverages and paraphernalia will be on site. Find a sitter and cut loose.

Every registration includes:

free event t-shirt

So quit yer bitchin’ about the price. We’re building a world-class event here.
(Just kidding. Same shitshow—better stuff.)

The course & timing (aka: how this actually works)

Open loop: 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM
This is your chance to pre-ride, scope lines, or course-walk and pretend you’re “studying conditions.”

Racing starts: 11:00 noon
Yes, for everyone.

Start times and final format will be confirmed day-of, because we won’t know what Mother Nature cooked up until about five minutes before we’re supposed to start.

The course is lap-based, roughly 1.0 mile per lap, depending on conditions and how mean we’re feeling.

Timing is handled by Eleven11 Timing, using plate-mounted chips. Once you get your plate, stay the hell away from the start line until your race.

Features, obstacles & questionable decisions

The course will include built structures, obstacles, and drops, all with time-consequential go-arounds.

Translation:

“You gotta go around it if you don’t wanna send it.”

No one is forced to ride any feature.
If you’re fast, you won’t need them.
If you’re not fast but you’re sendy—well… there’s your edge.

Capeche?

The course will be clearly marked with arrows and tape. It is the racer’s responsibility to know the route. Open loop starts at 9:00 AM for riding or walking the course.

Please do not stand on features at any time—especially during open loop or racing. We like you, and we’d like to keep it that way.

Each category  1st, 2nd, and 3rd place. No awards. Just bragging rights and a free t-shirt.
This is old-school racing: no swag, all brag. Run what ya brung.

We’re here for the course, the chaos, and bringing genuinely interesting racing back to New England. Show up with a good attitude and battle it out with a bunch of like-minded bike weirdos.

Costumes and ridiculous headwear are encouraged.

Bring your own spectators.

Team tents, parking & general “don’t be an idiot” info

  • Team tents welcome in the designated Get Ready Area (parking lot)
  • Plenty of parking on site
  • 10x10 tents allowed—must be weighted or staked
  • Dogs must be leashed
  • People must be fully clothed at all times (not our rule- just go with it)
  • Registration opens at 9:00 AM
    • Not 8:59 Seriously. No.
  • Waivers required
  • Anyone under 18 must have a parent/guardian signature
  • Porta-johns will be on site—use them
  • Helmets are mandatory for anyone pedaling a bike

Kelley Acres Speed Shop

2027 Winter Performance Training

10-Week Program 

Please read the information below carefully before selecting your in-person or at-home training option.

 

Program Overview

The 10-week Winter Performance Training Program begins the week of January 4, 2027  and ends the week of March 8, 2027

 

The Winter Session follows a progressive training plan building on the Fall Session The focus is on improving aerobic, threshold and anaerobic fitness by managing workout intensity progressively. Each week builds upon the previous week to prepare athletes for the 2027 outdoor season.

Monday and Wednesday: Speed-Focused Training

Thursday: Strength-Focused Training

Athletes who register for two in-person classes per week will receive a $50 discount.

Equipment Information

A cadence display on your bike computer is recommended. KASS cadence sensors may be available for use.

Important: KASS uses wheel-on trainers. If your bike has a thru axle, you must bring a compatible trainer thru-axle adapter.

Visit The Robert Axle Project for compatibility information.

Please bring:

  • Your bike

  • A water bottle

  • A towel—or two if you sweat heavily!

  • A heart-rate monitor is also recommended

KASS At-Home Training

The KASS At-Home option allows you to complete the Winter Performance Training workouts on your own schedule.

Two complementary workouts will be offered each week:

  • Speed Demon: Speed-focused training

  • Beast Mode: Strength-focused training

The workouts target different energy systems and are designed to work together as part of a balanced, progressive training plan.

The at-home workout package is $125 and includes Speed Demon and Beast Mode.

Workout files are available in the following formats:

  • .zwo for Zwift

  • .mrc for compatible training platforms

Workout files will be emailed each Monday.

Athletes are responsible for uploading the files and confirming compatibility with their chosen training platform. If you experience technical problems, please contact the support team for that platform.

Zwift: Importing Custom Workouts

TrainerRoad Support

Additional class information is available at www.kelleyacres.net.

Schedule Notes

Classes may occasionally be canceled because of inclement weather. Riders will be notified by email and will receive the scheduled workout to complete at home.

Registration Policies

Because each registration reserves a limited space in the program, registration fees are generally non-refundable once the session begins.

Missed classes are not refundable or eligible for a make-up class. An athlete may find a substitute and arrange reimbursement directly with that person.

If an injury prevents an athlete from completing the program, please contact KASS as soon as possible to discuss whether a transfer, credit, or other accommodation may be available.

The Central Coast Classico is a new, welcoming, non-competitive cycling festival celebrating the stunning roads, gravel, and coastal beauty of California's Central Coast. Launching in 2026, it replaced the beloved annual event Eroica California, building on decades of local riding heritage while introducing a fresh format focused on enjoyment of our landscapes and community.

This three-day celebration invites cyclists of all levels—vintage bike enthusiasts and modern road/gravel riders alike—to experience scenic, rewarding routes with food stops, mechanical support, live music, and great food. No racing, no pressure—just pure riding joy in one of California's most picturesque regions.

Join us for the Buddy Christian Memorial Bike Tour, a meaningful local fundraiser bike ride honoring law enforcement officers who have given their lives in the line of duty. This ride mirrors the spirit and purpose of the nationally recognized Police Unity Tour, while bringing that mission home to our local community.

Hosted by the Buddy Christian Foundation, this group ride follows a thoughtfully planned route connecting several local police departments. At each stop, riders will pause for a brief presentation honoring fallen officers, ensuring their sacrifice is remembered and their legacy preserved.

The ride will maintain an average pace of approximately 15 mph, making it accessible to experienced recreational cyclists. Participants should be physically prepared to meet this pace. For the sake of group safety, if you fall too far behind the pace, a SAG (Support and Gear) will transport you to the next stop. Participants can restart with the group. 

All proceeds from this event will directly support the Buddy Christian Foundation, helping fund and send local riders to participate in the Police Unity Tour, where officers and supporters from across the country ride to honor the fallen and support their families.

Ride with purpose. Ride in unity. Ride to remember.

  • Helmet (required)
  • Front and rear lights recommended
  • Hydration and nutrition appropriate for the distance

Ride Rules & Safety:

  • This is a group ride and will follow all traffic laws.
  • Riders must obey all traffic signals and ride predictably.
  • Helmets are mandatory for all participants.
  • Ride leaders will be present to assist and keep the group together.

Support:
This is a supported group ride with planned stops at local police departments. Basic assistance will be available, but riders should be capable of completing the route at the stated pace. 

Food and Drinks: 

Food and drinks will be provided at rest stops along the route. Riders with food allergies, dietary restrictions, or other health concerns should plan accordingly and bring what they need for the full ride. 

Weather Policy:
This event will be held rain or shine. In the event of severe or unsafe weather, updates will be provided to registered participants.

Refund Policy:
Registration fees are considered a donation and are non-refundable.

Who Can Ride:
This event is open to cyclists comfortable riding in a group at a steady pace of approximately 15 mph. E-bikes that would last the full distance, are welcomed!

Battle of Blue Licks ‘27


Note: Any  category with registration numbers too low to earn upgrade points may be combined with another category for a better field. This will be discussed with all riders in that category beforehand. Age groups that are not points earning may be combined for the starting wave and scored separately.

Please note: If you register for a category that has a low number and do not want to race with a combined wave, there will be no refund for this within two weeks of the event. It takes every racer showing up on race day to keep these events happening and grow the sport. Encourage a friend to come race with you!

3 Days of Racing

Friday Time Trial - Mercx style, plan to race the same equipment as you would in the road race. This is an attempt to keep things fair for traveling racers who cannot bring multiple bikes and to keep the playing field even. If you are a TT specialist and want to run specific gear and aren’t concerned about weekend points accumulation, let me know and we will work something out. The TT is a point to point beginning in Mt Olivet and ending at the bottom of the the climb to Turtleback. We plan on hosting a group ride from Turtleback to the start which is 6 miles or you can arrange a carpool/shuttle situation.

Saturday will be a Road Race with our favorite hosts, Turtleback Ridge Brewery. This will be a 21.5 mile course and your category will decide if you do 1,2 or 3 laps. 

Sunday is the Curtis Belcher Memorial Road Race, Curt was the owner of Kat Daddyz who unexpectedly passed in 2026. This will be a fundraiser for his wife and children. 31 mile course. Category decides if you race 1 or 2 laps.

Each day earns points and we will award the top 3 points in each category on Sunday

If you park off the gravel road in the grass we are not responsible for you getting stuck.

EventName: The Tour of St. Louis Omnium

EventNotes:
Doom 2027 | Sixth Edition

Doom returns for its sixth edition with a new start/finish in Fayetteville, Arkansas, and a return to the Boston Mountains. Two entirely new routes bring together some of the most iconic backcountry riding in the Arkansas Ozarks, revisiting the classics that helped shape the event while venturing into new corners of the region. The result is a fresh take on Doom, built around the same pursuit of exceptional mixed-terrain riding that has driven the event from the beginning.

Mount Sequoyah will serve as a home base for riders and supporters throughout the event.

Doom - DRAFT Route

422 Miles | 43k+ Feet of Vert | ~30 Miles Singletrack | 70% Unpaved

Doom 2027 DRAFT · Ride with GPS

A return to Doom classics from editions 1–4 alongside new terrain, singletrack, and notable hike-a-bike sections. Proper rowdy backcountry riding; what we call mountain bike gravel.

Buried in Boston - DRAFT Route

262 Miles | 24k+ Feet of Vert | ~25 Miles Singletrack | 70% Unpaved

Buried in Boston DRAFT · Ride with GPS

Deep into the Boston Mountains and back through Oark, where Doom's first two editions began. Doom classics, new ground, singletrack, and hike-a-bikes. Shorter than Doom, but no easy way out.

Bike Choice

We recommend a cross-country mountain bike with tires measuring 2.2 inches or wider. While singletrack makes up a relatively small portion of both routes, much of the remaining terrain is equally demanding, with rough, chunky backroads and steep gradients that favor durable, high-volume tires, mountain bike gearing, and more forgiving geometry. Modern gravel bikes continue to push the boundaries of what's possible, but we believe a mountain bike is the better choice for these routes, even for riders prioritizing speed and efficiency.

Event Schedule

More details will be shared with registered participants via email as the event approaches.

Thursday, March 18 | Puritan Coffee & Beer

  • 6:05 PM – Shakeout Ride / Thirsty Thursday

Friday, March 19 | Mount Sequoyah

  • 11:00 AM–8:00 PM – Rider Check-In
  • 7:00 PM – Rider Raffle (must be present to be entered)

Saturday, March 20 | Mount Sequoyah

  • 5:00 AM – Doom Grand Depart (422 Miles)
  • 6:00 AM – Buried in Boston Grand Depart (262 Miles)

Check-In: All riders should plan to check in on Friday to collect their rider materials, gremlin bell, and rental tracker if applicable. If you're unable to make the scheduled check-in window, please email us in advance so we can coordinate accordingly.

Event Headquarters & Lodging

Mount Sequoyah will serve as the headquarters for Doom 2027, with Parker Hall hosting rider check-in and serving as the start and finish location for both distances. The property offers a variety of onsite lodging options for riders and supporters.

Parker Hall at Mount Sequoyah
150 N Skyline Drive
Fayetteville, AR 72701

Onsite Lodging

Mount Sequoyah is offering a special room block for Doom participants at $100 per room, per night. Registered riders will receive the group booking code and reservation details in their confirmation email.

Parker Hall Rooms & Vehicle Camping | March 19

A limited number of additional overnight options are available at Parker Hall for Friday, March 19, the night before the Grand Depart.

  • Parker Hall Rooms: Private dorm-style rooms upstairs in Parker Hall with either two twin beds or two sets of bunk beds, an in-room sink, and access to shared bathrooms, showers, and a community kitchen. Vehicles can remain parked at designated public parking areas on Mount Sequoyah throughout the event.
  • Vehicle Camping: Guaranteed parking in the lot adjacent to Parker Hall, with access to the community kitchen, restrooms, and showers. No hookups, trailers, or vehicles longer than a Sprinter van. Vehicles may remain parked throughout the event. 

Both options are available as separate add-ons through the event registration page, subject to availability. Parker Hall rooms are not included in Mount Sequoyah's regular lodging reservations.

Self-Supported Riding

Doom is a self-supported event. Riders are responsible for their own resupply and equipment throughout the route, with no planned neutral aid stations or event-provided pickup services.

Over the years, local businesses, communities, and groups have occasionally provided additional hospitality along the routes, including places to sleep and sometimes food or other resources. Nothing of this nature is currently established for 2027. Should anything come together, details will be shared ahead of the event and made available to all riders.

Official event rules will be shared with registered participants ahead of the event.

Tracking

Live tracking is required for all participants. Riders may use their own compatible tracking device or rent one through our third-party tracking provider for an additional fee. Tracking allows friends, family, and the event team to follow rider progress throughout the course. Additional details regarding device compatibility, rentals, and tracking setup will be shared with registered participants as the event approaches.

Refunds

Full refunds are available through the end of February 2027. After that, riders are welcome to transfer their entry to another participant if they can find someone interested in taking their spot. Arranging the transfer is the rider's responsibility.

Price Increases

Registration is $100 through the end of December 2026. A single $25 price increase takes effect January 1, 2027, bringing registration to $125. All prices are before applicable taxes and registration fees.

Welcome to Redlands Strada Rossa XII: Your Ultimate Gravel Adventure!

 

Get ready for the 13th iteration of the legendary Redlands Strada Rossa (RSR)! Since its start in 2013, this event has been much more than just a ride—it's a not-for-profit charity event dedicated to supporting the beautiful open spaces in our community.

This year, we will once again offer two routes: a 50-mile and a 75-mile ride, offering riders a chance to experience the spectacular local trail network alongside our cyclists. Every entry directly benefits the Redlands and Crafton Hills Conservancies and The Bicycle Tree in Santa Ana, helping us preserve the incredible open space surrounding Redlands.

What to Expect: An Unpredictable Adventure

RSRXIII is set for Saturday March 20st, 2027.

The Course is a Secret (Until Right Before!): We know you're excited to see the route, but a core part of the RSR tradition is the element of surprise! We change the course every year to provide a fresh challenge and because winter trail conditions change constantly. To ensure we avoid muddy, rutted, or washed-out areas, we purposefully release the course map as late as possible—you can expect the final course files just 3 days before the event.

The course will be marked, but we strongly recommend loading the file onto your personal device as a backup for the safest adventure.

It’s an Adventure, Not a Race: Please remember, RSR is not timed and is definitely not a race. It’s a collective adventure! We provide SAG support and look forward to celebrating with you at the finish line with a complimentary meal.

Rain or Shine: There is no rain date—if the weather brings rain, consider it an extra dose of adventure! Please note that no refunds will be issued after March 2nd.

Event Day Logistics

We ask all participants to be courteous and safe on the course:

  • You will be sharing the road with vehicles and must always follow traffic laws.

  • Please yield the trail to all other users, including hikers and those on horseback, and extend the utmost courtesy to everyone you encounter.

Start Times:

  • 50 Mile Ride: 8:00 am

A Huge Thank You to Our Sponsors

This event is powered by our incredible sponsors and all-volunteer crew! Please support those who support our trails:

We can't wait to see you on the dirt for RSRXIII! What distance will you be conquering?

Registration will also be available at an increased fee on Saturday and Sunday, tell your friends to sign up now, they can still register.

 

COURSE DESCRIPTION

Who says Florida is flat? Centered in the rolling orange groves of Pasco & Hernando County, Gran Fondo Florida starts and ends at on Dade City Brew House 14323 7th St, Dade City, FL 33523. The race follows, in part, the proposed Olympic road race course that was part of Tampa’s bid to host the Summer Olympic Games.  It travels along rural rolling hills, past horse farms and crystal clear springs. Briefly going through Withlacoochee State Forest and the hills surrounding Brooksville, Florida. At the 89 mile mark you will enter a piece of US cycling history along Darby road, once home to the famous Darby Road Race that has seen the likes of Tour de France winner Laurent Fignon. This area is and has been the winter training site of some of the top triathletes in the world including members of the TIMEX team and the hometown of former US National Cycling team members Josh Thornton and Derek Wilkerson.

 

LOCAL CHARITY PARTNER

This event raises funds for Pasco County SRO Explorer Program. The School Resource Officer (SRO) Unit is composed of two squads that provide law enforcement services to schools countywide. The SRO Explorer Program provides services for those aged 14-21

Only the timed segments count.  Your overall, age group, and gender rankings are determined by your combined time for all timed segments on the route you choose. View Complete Rules and FAQ.

Tellico Grains Bakery
105 Depot Street
Tellico Plains, TN 37385

The Waucheesi Bike Event is wickedly sweet and includes three distances: the Wily 88, the Wondrous 63, and the 38 Special, crafted by Chris Joice.

Make no mistake, this event is just as challenging as it is beautiful. Cherohala Skyway, Cherokee and Nantahala National Forests provide all the goods—long climbs, fast descents, great forest roads, rowdy gravel, and amazing vistas. 

If you dare to try the 88-mile option, you’re looking at a stout 11,500+ feet of climbing, and a big day of mountain graveling.  The Classic 63-mile course is no joke, with 8,800+ feet, and is arguably, the perfect collection of Tellico gravel. Both routes include the Basin Gap and North River Road climbs, while the 88-mile course adds the spectacular climb to Farr Gap.

Back for 27' is the 38 Special, which offers a more sensible route, but plenty of scenery and it's fair share of climby gravel.  This gem leaves out the Basin Gap and North River climbs, but utilizes Tellico River Rd to access an exclusive "special" loop to Rafter Community and back.  

Riders must be finished by sunset. Therefore, we have the following time requirements for the 63 and 88 mile distances: 

  • 63 and 88-mile racers must reach the 24-mile split point by 1pm or you will be directed to the 38-mile route.
  • 88-mile racers must reach 45-mile split by 2:30pm or you will have to take the 63-mile route.
  • If you are completing the 88-mile course, you must have lights at rest stop 4 after 6pm.

Course Maps: All riders are responsible for downloading and using the provided maps to navigate the course. The course will not be marked. To download detailed course maps and gpx files, visit our website here.

Included: Police escorted neutral roll-out, four fully stocked aid stops, delicious post-race meal from Tellico Grains Bakery, and beverage.

Podiums: Podiums will be held for top three in each category* for each distance, and Overall Podiums (63 and 88 distances) for Male and Female will be Five-deep with Cash-Prizes for top 3!  Winners of each age/distance will receive a free-entry to next year's event(s).  *race director may combine categories for full podiums

T-shirts: Event t-shirts are $25. It's a high quality, super-comfy triblend that will quickly become your favorite tee. Order ahead to make sure you get yours!

Packet Pick-up: Packets must be picked up in person at Tellico Grains Bakery on either Saturday, 6-8pm or day of the event starting at 6am. 

Post-ride: All routes end back at Tellico Grains Bakery, where you'll enjoy wood-fired pizzas and craft beverage, while cheering on finishers, and celebrating the day!

The Waucheesi: Wicked, Wily & Wondrous.

Proudly presented by Caribbean Sports Organization, and sponsored by The Puerto Rico Tourism Company, La Épica Gravel Grinder® was designed to attract gravel cyclists from all corners of the globe, offering a stunning route that showcases the rugged beauty of Puerto Rico’s diverse terrain. Journeying through the rolling hills, the coastal plains, and the unique gravel roads of southern Puerto Rico, you will face an unforgettable challenge framed by the tropical allure of the Caribbean

We’ve carefully chosen a late march date to provide an ideal cycling getaway for cyclists who are wrapping up their winter, offering a perfect opportunity to start your riding season logging in plenty of kilometers in warm, sunny weather.  

We’ve crafted an event that will test your endurance while highlighting the best of Puerto Rico’s breathtaking landscapes and vibrant culture. Whether you chose to complete the two day “Grinder” main event or just come to ride one of the two daily events, this will be an adventure through one of the most beautiful regions in the Caribbean.  

Friday’s Gravel “Crit” will be an exhibition Gravel Criterium and promises to be an exciting preamble to the main event Saturday and Sunday. The “Crit” is perfect for those who love fast-paced competition and want to stretch their legs.

The first leg of the main event – “La Épica Gravel Grinder®” will take place on Saturday offering a taste of what’s to come. It will offer two options:

For those who come to compete in one of the OPEN categories this will be an 80Km ride. 

Those who are riding for recreational purposes have the option of doing the same 80km ride at a Non-competitive pace.

Sunday's second and final stage will be an 140Km ride for those who come to compete in one of the OPEN categories. 

Those who are riding for recreational purposes will, once again, have the option of doing then 140Km version of the route at a Non-competitive pace.

We can’t wait to see you in Ponce and welcome you to this extraordinary event.  

Get ready for an unforgettable experience at La Épica Gravel Grinder!  

Warm regards,  

Ernesto L. Collazo, MD - CEO - Caribbean Sports Organization, LLC

Welcome to the East Texas Showdown

Hosted at the Bullet Grill House in Point Blank, Texas, the East Texas Showdown brings together gravel racing, adventure cycling, and bikepacking across the remote pine forests of East Texas. Choose your route, choose your approach, and know this: however you ride your damn bike, you’ll be celebrated at the Hoedown!

Where We Ride

Texas doesn’t have much public land, but we make the most of what we’ve got. The routes explore forgotten roads in and around the Sam Houston and Davy Crockett National Forests, deep within the Texas Pine Curtain. Expect towering loblolly pines, quiet backroads, tiny rural communities, and locals wondering, “What the heck are y’all doing way out here?”

Why We Ride

ETS was created to be safe, fun, approachable, and community-driven. What began as a bikepacking event has grown into a family gathering where hundreds of friendships are formed and strengthened each year. We can’t wait to welcome everyone back in 2027.

Routes

The Showdown — Race

400 miles | 17,000 feet of climbing | 60% unpaved / 40% paved | Two national forests

A traditional, self-supported bikepacking race with awards for first, second, and third place. Remote roads, fast dogs, and an opportunity to look yourself square in your own damn face and find out what you’re made of.

100% East Texas.

The Slowdown — Race

273 miles | 11,000 feet of climbing | 60% unpaved / 40% paved | Two national forests

A shorter, but still rowdy, option for riders who want a little more time to enjoy the experience and maybe pet a dog or two. Riders are timed, with awards for first, second, and third place.

The Lowdown — Ride

Not a race | No timing | Maximum vibes

The Lowdown is a community-focused bikepacking ride for people who care more about the journey than the clock.

Lowdown riders can gather Friday evening at the designated group campsite at Ratcliff Lake for food, drinks, firewood, stories, and plenty of camaRADerie. Group camping is optional, but the more, the merrier.

Fun awards: Best Dressed | Best On-Course Photo | Raddest Bike

The Gravél Throwdown — Race

Choose between 69 and 42 mile routes through the infamous “Death Star” section of the Showdown course.

The 69 mile race is a three-loop burner beneath towering loblolly pines. The 42 mile option includes an out-and-back on one of our favorite roads anywhere in the Showdown Series: FS 202, better known as Golden Gravel Road. It’s so good, we promise you won’t mind riding it twice.

Both distances bring the self-supported spirit of bikepacking to gravel: no aid stations and no outside support—fix your own damn bike. However it goes, we’ll celebrate you at the Hoedown.

EventName: Basecamp Kitten Retreats: Catoctin Climbing Camp - Level 1
EventNotes:
Basecamp Kitten Retreats 2027: 
Catoctin Climbing Camp - Level 1
March 26 - March 28, 2027

An introductory, co-ed road cycling camp weekend for folks interested in practicing, training, and learning more climbing skills with Coach Jill Patterson. We’ll ride on both flat and hilly terrain while working on the skills that make a strong climber: durability and fitness, cadence management, pedaling dynamics, bike handling, descending, and braking. 

This “Level 1” climbing weekend will start & finish at Basecamp Lodge in Frederick, MD and include food, rides, clinics, workshops, training sessions, lodging, and more. Levels 2 and 3 camps will follow later in the year. Space is limited (20–25 participants total).

LOCATION: Basecamp Frederick Lodge - 9106 Hamburg Rd, Frederick, MD

REGISTRATION: $400 + lodging (optional)

A non-refundable $100 deposit is due upon registration. The remaining balance can be made as either 1 full payment or 2 separate payments (see payment schedule below): 

  • Balance Payment #1 - $150 (50%) due by February 1 , 2027
  • Balance Payment #2 - $150 (50%) due by March 1, 2027

CANCELLATION & REFUND POLICY:

The $100 deposit is nonrefundable. Participants may receive a full refund (excluding the non-refundable deposit and BikeReg service fee) before February 1, 2027 and a 50% refund (excluding the deposit and service fee) before March 1, 2027. There will be NO refunds issued after March 1, 2027. However, if the event is canceled prior to the start date, participants will have the option to receive a 50% refund (excluding the deposit and service fee) or a 100% entry credit (excluding the deposit and service fee) to be used toward future Dirty Kitten Productions events. Please consider all information provided when registering for this event and carefully read through the BikeReg registration insurance policy options before making your selection.  

BASECAMP KITTEN RETREAT PARTICIPANT EXPECTATIONS:

This is an inclusive, co-ed event open to all riders.

  • Read the Event Details and agree to all guidelines (including our DEI statement)
  • Schedule a bike tune-up before the event (call your local bike shop!)
  • Review the event outline and schedule (updated info will be provided)
  • Arrive on time and be prepared to ride each day (review the schedule for info)
  • Follow the rules of the road at all times when riding (Maryland Bike Law)
  • Act in a safe and respectful manner toward other participants
  • Prepare a personal "meal plan" for all on-your-own meals (unless otherwise specified)
  • Carry basic bike repair equipment on every ride (flat pack w/ tubes, pump, CO2, etc)
  • Make responsible choices in the weeks leading up to camp so as not to negatively affect other participants (i.e. take necessary health & safety precautions, schedule seasonal bike maintenance & repair, arrange accommodations, start packing early, plan your meals, stay up-to-date with local news & events, etc)
  • Contact Alex or Jill with questions, comments, or concerns prior to arrival: retreat@dirtykittengravel.com

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

- The total event fee includes rider support, bike safety & maintenance checks, skills clinics, training sessions, group activities, discussions, one group dinner, ride snacks, photos, swag, and some additional services (TBA).

Feel free to bring your own food and/or items to share and store at Basecamp Lodge throughout the weekend.

EventNotes:
Join us for our 4th annual Maine Maple Sunday Ride!

New for 2027, the ride will be on Saturday with a rain/snow day of Sunday.  

This is a loop that I've been doing for a few years with my buddies but I've decided it was time to share it with all!  It includes 60-ish miles of beautiful mid-coast Maine back roads (with a few a few stints on state roads) and stops at five sugar shacks and the famous Sheepscot General Store.  The route is 100% paved but has a bit of a spring classics feel because of the weather and general road conditions this time of year.  A road or gravel bike will be the ideal mode of transportation.  This year's loop will be a bit different, but you can check out last year's loop here:  https://www.strava.com/activities/8782628772 

Depending on your fitness level, and how many goodies you consume at the sugar shacks, the 60 mile participants should expect to be out anywhere from 3-6 hours.  There will be a short loop option as well.  Exact distance tbd, but it should be around 30 miles for anyone looking for a bit less challenge.  This loop only has one big climb, but dishes out just shy of 100' per mile of climbing to help you build your early season base!  

All registered participants will receive a gpx file (via e-mail) for both loops.  This ride is a go rain or shine!  In the off chance of extremely inclement weather forcing us to cancel, registered riders will have the option to defer to next year's ride, transfer the registration to the The Nelson Farm Weekend, the Fon Solo gravel ride in the fall or to donate the funds to the Schmid Preserve. 

All proceeds go to support the trails in and around the Schmid Preserve in Edgecomb. 

Brought to you in part by our friends at Six Rivers NEMBA.  

 

We have merch available!  Head on over to Hubnotic and pick up a few goodies.. https://www.hubnotic.com/collections/maine-maple-sunday-ride

EventName: Athens Physical Therapy Firefly Trail Ticket to Ride 2027
EventNotes:
Join us for our 16th Annual Ticket to Ride up and down the future route of the Firefly Trail on Saturday, March 27, 2027. 

We are proud and honored that Athens Physical Therapy has returned as the Presenting Sponsor for the 2027 Firefly Trail Ticket to Ride! We can't say enough good things about Dr. Chris and Stephanie Doerr, the staff at APT, and the amazing work they do for their patients, the community, and the Firefly Trail. Thank you, APT! Visit their website at https://athenspt.com/. 

Show your ride wristband, and riders over 21 yrs. old, will receive one free pour of beer in Athens with our new beer partner Athentic Brewing Co.,108 Park Avenue! In Union Point receive a free sample of Athletic Brewing Company Non-Alcoholic beer! 

All proceeds benefit the work of Firefly Trail Inc. to promote the completion of a 39-mile multipurpose trail connecting multiple counties and communities in Northeast Georgia between Union Point and Athens.

Choose to register starting at 8AM for mass start at 10AM from:
• Dudley Park, Dudley Park Rd, in Athens
• Winterville Depot, corner of S Main & Parkview, Winterville
Or register starting at 7AM for mass start at 9AM from:
• Union Pharmacy, 624 Sibley Ave, Union Point

Paved Routes:
The full out-and-back course on paved roads between Athens and Union Point is approx. 82 miles with on-route support and fully stocked SAG stops (including restrooms) every 8-13 miles in Athens, Winterville, Crawford, Maxeys, and Union Point. Because this is an out-and-back route, riders can tailor their ride length by simply turning around. This on-road ride features the lowest-traffic paved roads we could find close to the historic corridor of the Georgia Railroad Athens Branch. These routes use completed sections of the Firefly Trail in Athens-Clarke County, Winterville, Maxeys, Greene County, Woodville and Union Point. Riders who enjoy flatter terrain will especially enjoy the route from Union Point to Maxeys or from Winterville to Crawford. Options as short as 15 miles are available, making this a perfect ride for cyclists of all interests and abilities.

Ride With GPS routes: A new section on the Athens to Winterville Firefly Trail  – Hancock Road to Taylor Lane – was opened 7.24.26. The routes below will be updated to reflect this new section.

To be updated for 2027:

·         Up to 67 miles: Winterville to Union Point and back: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54050125
·         Up to 82 miles: Union Point to Athens and back: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54052763

•    Athens-Winterville: 14.8 miles
•    Athens-Crawford: 37.6 miles
•    Athens-Maxeys: 57.0 miles
•    Winterville-Crawford: 22.8 miles

Gravel routes from 2026. Updates for 2027 may be made to these routes prior to the ride.
For those with an adventurous spirit, two gravel rides are back by popular demand!

•    66.1 miles: Union Point to Crawford & Back – https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53793829 (Rev 2.19.26)

Board member and Specialized trainer Lisa Baynes has mapped out these routes, aligning them near the highway to show how Firefly Trail is a great connector to all these beautiful back roads. Both routes will use all 7 miles of the completed, paved Firefly Trail in Greene County, including within the cities of Union Point and Woodville.

Gravel rides are self-supporting, which means there will not be vehicle support. It will be critical to have the route on your computer or a buddy with the route, and to carry tools should repairs be necessary. The routes will be as close to Georgia Highway 77 as possible.

The purpose of our event:
Firefly Trail Inc. is a 501(c)(3) Georgia non-profit corporation working with local communities and other partners to build and maintain the Firefly Trail, a 39-mile rail-trail on or near the historic corridor of the Georgia Railroad Union Point/Athens Branch. Funds raised by Ticket to Ride support the work of our all-volunteer Board of Directors, volunteers, and professional Trail Development Coordinator. Mission-critical work includes engaging the public and assisting trail communities with applying for grants and raising matching funds for design, engineering, property acquisition, construction and maintenance. To learn more, visit www.fireflytrail.com.
