EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Lab Sessions/MARCH 29-31
EventNotes:
Sharpen the skills that matter most. TRS Skills Labs are focused, two-hour sessions dedicated to the techniques riders struggle with most. Pick your biggest challenge, or complete all three Labs to build confidence and become a more complete rider.
 
TRS Skills Lab- Cornering & Berms 

The fastest way to become a better rider is to corner better. In this two-hour Skills Lab, you'll create an understanding of the techniques that create traction and confidence through every type of turn.

 

The Ride Series “Cornering Matrix” will allow you to engage the technique in a safe environment while focusing on proper body position and inputs. You'll leave carrying more speed, using less energy, and feeling more in control in every corner.

 

You'll work on:

Body position 

Vision and line choice

Braking strategy and timing

Creating traction and maintaining control

Building speed through corners

 

TRS Skills Lab - Drops 

Drops SHOULD be intimidating. That’s your brain trying to keep you safe. Relying on instinct is generally what gets people in trouble. Creating proper instincts that will carry you through most drops is what this two-hour Skills Lab will do. It’s designed to help you understand the techniques behind smooth, controlled drop-offs so you can ride them with confidence.

 

Through progressive features, focused drills, and individualized coaching, you'll develop proper body position, timing, and bike control while learning how to assess features and choose the right approach. Every rider progresses at their own pace in a supportive, low-pressure environment.

 

You'll work on:

Body position and timing

Footwork to help create stability 

Feature assessment and speed management

Smooth, controlled landings

Progressing to larger drops as skills improve

TRS Skills Lab - Jumps 

Build the foundation for safe, confident jumping in this two-hour Skills Lab. Rather than chasing bigger airtime, we'll focus on the techniques that make every jump more controlled and consistent.

You'll work through progressive drills with personalized coaching to develop proper takeoff mechanics, body position,  and landing technique. By understanding the "why" behind each movement, you'll leave with the confidence and skills to continue progressing long after the session ends.

You'll work on:

Takeoff mechanics

Body position throughout the jump

Pumping and generating lift

Bike control

Smooth, controlled landings

Progressive feature selection

TRS Skills Lab Combo - Complete all three Labs to build confidence and become a more complete rider.

The Mine Creek Gravel Battle offers a fantastic blend of adventure, history, and sport, allowing participants to ride through the historic terrain of the Battle of Mine Creek while also learning about the dramatic events that unfolded there in 1864. For cyclists, it’s a way to test their skills on a challenging and scenic route, while for history buffs, it’s an immersive experience that deepens their connection to the American Civil War. Combining these elements, it’s a memorable way to honor the past while enjoying the present!

Gainesville TBC, now in its second year, is a tour of four of the Taco Bell locations within Gainesville, FL and surrounding areas. There will be six total options available, Diablo (gravel+) and Fire (road) versions of the Century, Half Century, and new this year, Quarter Century. 

Athletes should be ready to have a Taco-Tastic time drinking Baja Blast, eating Chalupa Supremes all while pedaling with friends. Similar to last year a point based scoring system will be enacted to allow participants to enjoy the time they are on the bike rather than racing directly to the finish, where Taco Bell items consumed are worth way more than the miles traveled. 

For those interested in a steeper challenge, athletes may compete for the FKT on this route, which obviously stands for Fastest Konceivable Time.

The event ticket will include access to the entire collection of routes, the grand depart, and any TBC events on Friday, April 3rd.

Join us for the 2nd Annual Straight Up Gravel as we race the rugged gravel roads of America’s first national river — The Buffalo! Be prepared for remote, chunky gravel beneath a canopy of trees that winds through a national park, creating a straight up one-of-a-kind gravel event.

The 75-miler is a true climber’s delight, featuring two major climbs: one at 2.5 miles with an 8.2% average gradient, and another at 1.6 miles, also averaging 8.2%. While those two climbs account for 1,800 ft of elevation gain, that still leaves 5,200 ft distributed throughout relentless “rollers”. There will be 3 aid stations along this course at miles 27, 43, & 56. Be prepared for remote back-country riding. 

The 50-miler offers much of the same rugged terrain, minus the two major climbs, but still includes plenty of uphills—around half- to one-mile stretches at 8% gradients. This route will have 1 aid station at mile 27. 

The 25-mile route is smoother and more beginner-friendly while still providing a rewarding challenge.

The UNDEAD Death Ride is loosely based on the routes of the historic Flint Hills Death Ride. Discover Gravel LLC is not associated in any way with the original FHDR. I simply am a fan of local gravel history. First and foremost the UDR is a group ride out in the Flint Hills. 

The UDR is a completely unsupported gravel adventure consisting of a 70 mile loop. The 70 mile loop has two 35 mile legs. Riders may start in Madison or Matfield Green.  Note if you are only riding one direction, half the distance, you must arrange your own transport back to your vehicle.

Exact parking and starting locations will be made known closer to the ride. Keep in mind Matfield Green has extremely limited resources. I am considering setting up a basic hydration station for the turn around.

Started in 2017, this very popular event returns with three great distances and routes to choose from!  The start finish is from our hosts property at the Leesville Cemetery Association.  We'll have a neutral roll-out for all distances at 9am.

There's a great mix of smooth and fast gravel, with a hint of sand and even short chunky gravel sections.  You'll enjoy quiet twisting roads and tree canopies in the friendliest little part of Texas!  Two neutral hydration stations on course.  Choose the right distance for your abilities, to be back in Leesville before 2:30pm.

We'll be waiting for you at the finish line celebration with lunch benefiting the Leesville Cemetery Association with music and drinks with all your gravel friends!  Great awards on our Houston Fish Law podiums!  Don't miss a great day of gravelly fun!

All registered participants will receive an info email first thing Friday morning before the event.  All riders should start the ride with a minimum of 2 water bottles or a hydration pack, all needed nutrition, and a repair kit for flat tires and minor mechanical needs.  Riders should also carry a cell phone for emergency calls, and have the gps files loaded onto their bike computer or phone in the Ride With GPS app for navigation.  The routes are not marked.

Please see our website and facebook page for more info!  www.capitalcityracingtexas.com  www.facebook.com/capitalcityracingtexas.com/  www.instagram.com/capitalcityracingtexas/

See you out there!

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics/JUMP Essentials & ADV JUMP Technique: BENTONVILLE APRIL 3RD
EventNotes:
Are YOU ready to invest in your riding? Be safer, more confident, have more fun because you KNOW what needs to happen on the trail and you're familiar with how to execute. This session isn't for everyone, we're quite ok admitting that. This is for riders that are ready to be in a setting with coaches that actually have relevant experience in doing AND teaching the subject matter. We GUARANTEE you'll leave this session with the tools needed to become the rider you've always wanted to be. 

Founders and Lead Coaches Rob and Rich Drew will break down all of the nuance behind success when jumping. From groomed takeoffs to janky rock kickers, the brothers will provide deep insight into what needs to happen, how it needs to happen, and when! 

 

JUMP Essentials Session:

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get plenty of reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
 

ADVANCED JUMP TECHNIQUES: 
Are you ready to take your jumping to the next level? This is the session to make it happen! Refinement is the key here and breaking it down deeper with bigger jumps and more in depth video analysis is the way to make it happen. 

RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

A checkpoint-style ride to the hidden gems of Chittenden County

Here’s the situation, it’s April 4th, the buds are budding, the days are getting longer, and you’re looking to dust off the bike after a long hibernation. Well, your friends at Jericho Dirt have cooked up the next iteration of Unrouted. 
 

Here’s the deal, there will be a start and finish location, but no set route. A few days before the event all participants will be sent GPS coordinates and clues for checkpoints at some of our favorite places, where books are hidden. At each checkpoint you will need to find the book, rip out the page corresponding to your number plate. Once you have collected all of the pages, you return to the finish destination and turn them in for a finish time. You’re free to take any route you like and connect the checkpoints in any order. Want to add in a scenic detour or favorite shortcut, go for it. The only rules are: you must complete the course under your own power on one bike (no uber, no bus rides, no bike swaps), follow all laws, and respect private property, trail, or road closures. 


Bike choice and route choice are half the challenge. While most races will tell you exactly where to go and what bike you must ride, this format leaves the choice up to you. There will checkpoints that favor a road bike, while others may favor a gravel bike, and maybe one or two where you want a MTB. The route you choose can make one type of bike preferable over another. Some might choose to ride a road bike and hike any single track they encounter, others might choose the comfort and capability of a mountain bike. Generally a gravel bike is likely the most efficient, but that may differ based on your individual route and skills. 

There will be a long option, expect 55-75 miles, and a short option with fewer checkpoints, 25-40 miles. You can ride with as many friends as you like or roll solo. 

Once you make it to the finish, with or without all your pages, you will be greeted by a local hotdog and beer from Lucy and Howe brewery, included in your entry. Feel free to hangout and share adventure stories with your fellow riders.

Event rules

You Gotta Fight For Your Right to Party

Meet The Mix Tape.  It's not a gravel ride.  It's not a road ride.  It's not a mountain bike ride.  It's not a gran fondo.  It's not a race.  Well it is a race... if you want it to be a race.  But you don't have to race.  But you can totally race.  So, it's kind of a gran fondo.

The Mix Tape is our answer to the lack of something different down our way.  We wanted something that's as challenging as you want to make it with a little bit of everything.  Since we don't have many hills we had to get creative.  So we designed you a rolling party that covers pavement, light trails, fire roads, a little single track, and some challenging tech that's brief but impactful.  What all of this means is that there's no perfect bike for this.  On the roads you'll hate your mountain bike and when you're climbing The Ledge you'll be wishing you had it.  So we feel that the perfect bike for this is the one with drop bars and the biggest tires that fit.  But you decide what works for you.  Just don't bring your road bike.  You won't get far and you will hate us when really you only have yourself to blame.

The course will be provided via a GPS file.  We will lightly mark some sections but know from past years that those markings may "evaporate" so you cannot rely on them.  For those of you racing, the Strava segments will be marked, hopefully.  The entire course is not a race, only those segments.  This encourages everyone to enjoy the event and party on, together.  It also discourages racing through intersections and traffic signals.  Obeying the rules of the road are important for safety and the future of the event.

Course maps and navigation files get emailed to participants just before the event and are not posted online.  We change it a little every year.  Sometimes we change it quite a bit!

This event is capped at whatever we're told until we prove to the towns that you'll ride through that we're not jerks.  Participants of previous years get a password to register early before registration opens to the public.  Sometimes this will sell out the event before it actually opens.

On My Darkest Days I Wear My Brightest Colors    

April in New England can be a mixed bag of conditions.  It could be hot, cold, or wet.  It could be hot, cold, AND wet.  Who knows?  You'll need to dress for changing conditions.  For visibility on the road sections every participant is recommended to run a rear tail light for added safety.  We also recommend bright colored clothing.

Everybody's Looking For Something   

This event isn't about the prizes, or the swag.  It's about the journey.  But dammit the prizes and swag are sweet too.

Here's how getting competitive works:  You have to run a GPS recording device capable of uploading to your Strava account through your phone when you finish.  We will not have computers for you to upload through because that did not work out in any year.  You can also run Strava on your phone.  Competitive riders have 5 hours to complete the course and upload and we post the results at 2:30pm.  There are 6 timed and marked segments, broken into three categories for awards.  Riders get their times of each category combined.  We award one male and one female winner of each category.  You can only win one category so in the event of someone sweeping all of them we award second place the prize.

ROADIE (tbd):  Combination of timed road segments

CLIMBER (tbd):  Combination of timed off road climbing segments

SHREDDER (tbd):  Combination of timed off road trail segments

MIX MASTER (tbd):  Combination of all timed segments

I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For

Not convinced that this is for you?  Ask someone who's come before, but it might be sold out by the time you do.

Course maps and navigation files get emailed to participants just before the event and are not posted online.

The route is 44.5 miles and features 2023 feet climbing.

For Those About To Rock We Salute You

This event is years in the making.  Hours of concept, arguing about the route, finding a venue, planning police details, town meetings, food, etc.  We do it for you, because we love you.  And we have to fight for it every single year.  Now get out there and crush this thing.

We are excited that Blount Fine Foods is allowing us to start finish and have an awesome after party afterwards. Your registration includes not only the great ride thru the Fall River Bioreserve and the Freetown Forest, but you will get a water bottle, T-shirt, Aid Stations stocked up with Skratch Labs products, the opportunity for some cool swag via Strava segment, a beer from Berkley Beer and a meal from Bount Clam Shack food truck!

 Refunds & Transfers

We're not jerks and we believe that a "no refunds policy" isn't a very encouraging thing to get you to commit to an event in advance.  So we give refunds up until 2 days before online registration closes, because that's plenty of time for someone else to take your place.  You just have to email us with a legit reason that isn't, "I don't like the weather forecast".  We also allow you to transfer your entry to another racer anytime up until online registration closes.  This costs an additional $5.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: DROP ESSENTIALS & DROP PROGRESSION APRIL 4TH
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

DROP ESSENTIALS: TRS Ground School  

Welcome to a world where Physics, Gravity, and the engineering of your bike are embraced to help guide you off drops like never before. It's not rocket science, it's rational thought manifesting in you being more confident and landing drops with more stability than you ever thought possible. In this session, we hone in on HOW to create that stability and here's some pertinent info…stability is a benefit EVERYWHERE! 

DROP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and Slaughter Pen Skills Park 

This session builds on the Drop Essentials and it's all about creating a deep understanding of HOW to execute the WHAT in any drop scenario.This is curated in our Ground School environment with specific implements that will allow you to execute multiple reps to create solid motor patterns. 

 Use of slo mo video feedback will have you growing confidence at a rapid rate. From there, it's time to head over to the Skills Park to dial it on multiple features. This is where the confidence is married with a newfound ability to work through the mental side of the equation. No guess work, no “just sending it", only conscience confidence in the what and how!  


This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: Bentonville Junior XC Race Camp April 5/6
EventNotes:
Join Ride Series founder and former USA Cycling Junior Development Coach Rich Drew for a two-day intensive camp focused on translating high-level technical skills into faster, more efficient race performance.

Designed specifically for competitive XC athletes that have high level aspirations, this camp challenges riders to refine the small details that create meaningful gains on course. Through focused skill development, race-specific application, and slow-motion video analysis, athletes will work to improve efficiency, maintain momentum, and make better decisions when the pressure is on. The 5 to 1 coach/rider ratio ensures a high level of one on one attention. 

Topics Covered:

  • Dialing in body position to maximize efficiency across varying terrain and race situations
  • Using heel position and pressure to improve control and conserve energy
  • Breaking down corners effectively to increase entry confidence and exit speed
  • Racecraft application: Developing strategies to adapt to changing race situations
  • Minimizing the impact of technical features while maintaining speed and momentum
  • Jumping dynamics specific to XC racing: Managing energy and landing efficiently to carry momentum
  • Maximizing efficiency across all technical elements to improve overall race performance
  • Slow-motion video analysis to identify, evaluate, and refine technique in real time

Athletes will leave with a deeper understanding of how to apply technical skills strategically, conserve energy, and turn small improvements into faster, more consistent race performance.

EventNotes:
MILE ZERO 

Delta Outdoor Festival 

 

RIDE • RUN • PADDLE  • BIRD

 

Mile Zero is a weekend celebration of the Arkansas Delta’s beautiful landscape. Formerly known as the Delta Grind, this rebrand reflects a new chapter rooted in Helena’s identity as the "gateway to the Delta"—where trails, rivers, history, and culture converge. Helena, one of Arkansas's most historic and significant Mississippi River ports, is a city with a deep and complex history. 

 

Join us for a rally-style celebration blending world-class riding and running with birding and paddling opportunities that highlight the region’s vibrant soul: live music, local food, and heritage. Here is a slide show to get you fired up to register.

 

ADVENTURE • CULTURE • COMMUNITY

 

“Mile Zero is more than an outdoor festival — it’s a strategic step toward positioning Helena as a hub for recreation, culture, and community vitality,” — Ammen Jordan, Director of studioDRIFT. “Our goal is to make outdoor recreation accessible to all. Through partnerships with local public schools and the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail Project, we are breaking down barriers, fostering community growth, and enhancing the quality of life for residents and visitors alike.”

 

WEEKEND SCHEDULE 

 

Friday, April 9: Shakeout & Socialize

Kick off the weekend at Delta Dirt (430 Cherry St)

  • 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM: Social Spin (10 - 25 miles, mixed route) - Free
  • 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM: Running Tour of Helena (2-3 miles, murals & Civil War history) - Free
  • Evening: Art show and music at 430 Cherry St
  • Bonus: Head over to the Juke Joint Festival in Clarksdale, MS

 

 

  

Sunday, April 11: Explore & Restore 

  • 8 AM – 12 PM: Guided Birdbiking
    • Free guided excursion during peak migration, full plumage and song.
  • 9 - 10 AM: Birding Basics at Storm Creek Lake Nature Trailhead
    • Join a park interpreter in a 1-mile hike to discover the joy of birding on Storm Creek Trail. With early spring migration, this is a wonderful time to spot colorful visitors such as warblers, Orioles, and buntings. All ages welcome. Binoculars and field guides will be available while supplies last. Wear sturdy shoes, bring water, and don’t forget insect repellent.
  • 8 AM – 12 PM: Guided Nature Walk
    • Habitat Harry will point out the vibrant wildlife and stunning scenery that make this landscape so legendary. ($20)
  • 9 AM: Casual Group Ride/Run from Delta Dirt (430 Cherry St)
    • Free, no drop, casual, not to be missed
  • 10 AM – 3 PM: Buck Island Canoe Adventure with Quapaw Canoe Company
  • 12 - 5 PM: Pedal and Paddle Tour  - Guided bike and kayak tour led by Delta Heritage Trail park interpreter.
    • Meet at the Barton visitor center and  caravan to Old Town Lake. 8-mile bike ride followed by 1.5 hour guided kayak tour. All equipment is included in the registration fee and no kayaking experience is necessary.
      • Limited space; preregistration required.
      • Call (870) 572-2352
      • Adults - $26.00; Children (10-12 y.o.)  - $16.00
  • 3 – 4 PM: Watercolor by the Water’s Edge @ Bear Creek Day Use Area
    • Join a park interpreter for a relaxing lakeside watercolor session. All skill levels welcome. Supplies are limited or bring your own. Capture the beauty of the water’s edge with color and creativity  (Free) 

 

SATURDAY ROUTE OPTIONS 

  • Cycling Routes - view on RideWithGPS
  • Running/Walking Routes - view on RideWithGPS
  • Bikepacking to the event? Here's a collection of regional routes

  

WHAT YOU WILL EXPERIENCE

  • Rolling topography unlike anywhere else in the Arkansas Delta 

  • Remote routes winding through rugged hills and hardwood forests 

  • Historic farming communities with rich blues music and cultural 

  • An adventure that flows like a true expedition — varied terrain, deeply scenic and endlessly rewarding 

 

WHY THIS ADVENTURE IS UNIQUE 

  • A true regional destination with elements that speak to your wandering souls

  • Long distances through unusual terrain

  • Fascinating landscapes with geological and cultural storytelling

  • Remote stretches with resupply and aid stations punctuating the effort

  • A broader purpose: community impact and rural reinvention 

  • For riders who chase  epics that matter, this is a place where miles and meaning meet.

 

 WHAT TO EXPECT

  • Routes are Unmarked
    • You MUST have a GPS app or printed directions
  • Zero Waste
    • Bring your own cup/bottle/hydration pack.
    • Water jugs will be available on the course.

  • Raffle tickets for a brand-new Specialized Sirrus (MSRP $850) are still available.
    • Every ticket you buy gets us closer to our $5,000 community goal.

  • More Options: King Biscuit Blues Festival Lodging List

  

TOP 10 THINGS TO DO IN HELENA

  1. Delta Cultural Center Museum: Music heritage (9am-5pm).
  2. Harbor View Trail: One-mile loop in Helena River Park. Link
  3. DIY Mural Tour: Explore city-wide art on wheels or foot. Link
  4. History Sites: African American & Confederate Cemeteries.
  5. Big River Loop Trail: Visit Buck Island Beach. Link
  6. Delta Dirt Distillery: Nation’s only Black-owned farm-to-bottle distillery.
  7. Delta Heritage Trail: Log miles and spot migratory birds.
  8. Delta Fish Market: World-famous fried catfish (10am-8pm).
  9. History Buff Tour: Civil War and Underground Railroad landmarks. Link
  10. DIY Paddling: Rent gear via phone at Mississippi River State Park. 

 

EVENT PARTNERS 

The entire community of Helena-West Helena 

Ecological Design Group

The Ozark Foundation

The RIDE Conway // Thrive, Inc. // Mississippi River State Park

 

 

WHY HELENA?

Originally thriving as a primary steamboat stop and the center of a prosperous cotton and timber empire, Helena’s geography at the southern foot of Crowley’s Ridge made it a strategic cornerstone of the Delta. Over time, the decline of river-based commerce and the mechanization of agriculture forced the community to reinvent itself. Today, a new economic growth strategy focused on heritage tourism, outdoor recreation, and the arts is transforming the community. 

 

However, like many rural communities in the region, the city is facing compounding demographic and economic challenges. The population has experienced a sharp decline and is struggling with the outmigration of its workforce and youth. The area faces both a consistently high poverty rate and the shortest life expectancy in Arkansas — nearly five years less than the national average. 

 

 

CROWLEY’S RIDGE GRAVEL TRAIL?

The development of the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail is a critical component of this revitalization effort, serving to both improve the quality of live and serve as a regional economic engine. Crowley’s Ridge is a unique geological anomaly — an island of adventure rising up to 250 feet above the sorrounding Delta farmland — offering an experience that is entirely distinct. By formalizing and expanding routes and natural surface trails along the ridge, we are creating a world-class recreational asset that capitalizes on the global trends in outdoor recreation.

Get ready for some of the best gravel roads in the Southeast! The Desoto National Forest has long been known for its vast road network and challenging Ragland Hills on the North side of the region. Riders will have the chance to take on courses ranging in length from 30 miles all the way to a full 100 miles. There is very, very little pavement on the course and the gravel ranges from hardpacked and fast to chunky and loose rock. 

Start/Finish Location: The intersection of Highway 29 & FS 312 just South of New Augusta is the location of the Start/Finish area for this year's race. There is ample parking, and overnight dispersed camping is permitted in the Desoto National Forest. While we have enjoyed the creature comforts of the Armed Forces Museum, we want to get back to the roots of gravel racing. 

Course Overview: 100-mile riders will cross through three counties (Perry, Greene and Forrest) while passing through the Leaf River Wildlife Management Area, Desoto National Forest and Camp Shelby Joint Forces Training Area.

All courses will get to experience portions of the Camp Shelby Joint Forces Training Area, and it is not uncommon to see National Guard units exercising in the many open areas along the course. You'll also get to experience a wide array of wildlife. It's not uncommon to see deer, turkeys, wild hogs, and a variety of snakes (including our namesake Eastern Diamondback Rattlesnake). 

And don't let our Southern latitude fool you, the 100-mile course packs approximately 4,500' of climbing while the 100K course comes in at approximately 2,800' of elevation gain. 

 

 

 

Aid Stations: Riders can expect to encounter multiple aid stations with water and a variety of snacks along their routes as follows (subject to change)

100 Mile - Mile 15, Mile 40, Mile 55, Mile 75 

100K - Mile 15, Mile 40

50K - Mile 15, Mile 25

 

Drop Bags: Two (2) Drop Bag opportunities for 100 milers and One (1) Drop bag opportunity for 100K. These WILL NOT return to the Start/Finish area until after race is complete and aid stations are shut down for other riders on course.

Awards: Awards will be given to all riders placing in the top three of their respective categories.

Time Limit: We offer a VERY generous 12-hour time cut-off for 100 mile and 100K riders. 

Results/Timing: Race will be chip timed with race results being updated and available throughout the day. QR code and link will be available on Friday, April 10th.

SAG: You are responsible for YOU. While we will be running a SAG wagon later in the day it is imperative that you carry the tools you need for basic bike repair (tube, plugs, CO2, master link, etc.). There will be phone numbers printed on the back of each bib for non-emergency assistance. For ALL emergencies it is recommended that you call 911!

Your Race Directors: This is a joint venture between South Mississippi Trail Alliance and Hub City Velo, both of which are cycling related non-profits based in the Hattiesburg area. All money raised from this event will stay in the community to support cycling and recreation related causes.

Are you ready to experience the other side of Putnam County gravel?  Get Buried is Putnam County's UNDERGROUND gravel race, giving you the chance to ride the CHUNKY and STEEP stuff on the western side of town.  

Always on the Saturday of Easter Weekend, Get Buried is a gravel race that pits you against others on a challenging 46 mile course (31 mile short course option).  The route features some of the more challenging hills and segments - including the great climbs and decents around Fallen Rock Campground, the Fern Cliff Nature Preserve area, and - the always excruciating - WASHOUT climb!

This year the ride includes a $70 registration fee that will allow every rider to complete an online waiver form digitally.  Part of your registration fee will go to support the family of Steve Williamson, a good cycling friend we lost a few years ago.  

If you know about Get Buried … well, you know.  It's gloriously difficult.  But still fun.  The best is the pre-ride coffee and the post-ride brew with tales of all the suffering.  Created as its very own “spring classic," the ride features an iconic climb into the Boone Hutcheson Cemetery, a long 15% incline that gives us our tag line:  “by the time you get here, you might already be dead!”

Come on out and join us for the ninth edition of Get Buried Putnam County!

Femmes Teams Event

For women of all ages and abilities, this is racing reimagined. Form a team of three or more and experience the camaraderie, teamwork, tactics, and fun that make cycling unforgettable.

Gather your friends, sisters, daughters, mothers, or riding partners. Sign up, ride together, and be part of a movement that's bringing more women to the start line.

Femmes Team Competition FAQ

Q: Are there team discounts?
A: No. Team discounts are not offered.

Q: How many riders can be on a team?
A: Teams can be any size. However, only your top three finishers count toward the team score.

Q: How are teams scored?
A: Each rider earns points equal to their finishing place (1st = 1 point, 2nd = 2 points, etc.). Your team's score is the combined total of your top three finishers. The team with the lowest score wins.

Example:

  • Team A: 4th, 8th, 15th (plus one DNF) = 27 points
  • Team B: 2nd, 7th, 20th (plus three additional finishers) = 29 points

Winner: Team A

Q: What if a rider doesn't finish?
A: Riders may DNF, but at least three team members must cross the finish line for the team to be eligible for awards.

Q: Can we do a relay?
A: No. Every rider must complete the full course.

Q: Are there age-group categories?
A: No. All Femmes Teams compete together regardless of age.

Q: How do we register as a team?
A: During registration, you'll answer a required question where you'll enter your team name. There is also an optional "Team Name" field in your registration profile.

Q: Does everyone need to register at the same time?
A: No. Team members can register and pay individually. Just be sure everyone enters the exact same team name during registration. .

Q: Can team members ride different courses?
A: No. All team members must compete on the same course

Q: If I place in the Femmes competition and also win my age group, will I receive awards for both?
A: No. Femmes is a separate competition. If you place in the Femmes standings, you will be removed from the age group results and will only be eligible for Femmes awards.

Weather Monitoring & Response Plan

The safety of participants, spectators, volunteers, staff, contractors, and public safety personnel is the highest priority of the event. While varying weather conditions are an inherent part of road cycling, extreme weather can create conditions that place individuals at unnecessary risk. ViM Racing reserves the right to modify, delay, shorten, suspend, or cancel the event at any time if weather conditions are determined to present an unacceptable safety risk.

 

Weather Monitoring:

Beginning at least 72 hours prior to the event, ViM Racing will continuously monitor weather forecasts and environmental conditions. Weather monitoring includes, but is not limited to:

  • Daily review of National Weather Service forecasts and local weather reports.
  • Monitoring for excessive heat or cold.
  • Monitoring for thunderstorms, lightning, hail, freezing rain, snow, or other hazardous precipitation.
  • Monitoring for high wind conditions that may affect rider safety.
  • Monitoring wildfire danger, Red Flag Warnings, smoke conditions, and any environmental hazards that may impact the course or surrounding communities.
  • Inspection of course conditions, including cattle guards, water crossings, erosion, washouts, and other hazards resulting from weather.
  • Consultation with rider representatives and local emergency management officials to incorporate athlete and public safety perspectives into operational decisions.

 

Weather Response:

Based on forecasted or observed conditions, ViM Racing may implement one or more of the following actions:

  • Continue to monitor conditions with no operational changes.
  • Modify portions of the course to avoid hazardous areas.
  • Shorten one or more race distances.
  • Delay or adjust start times.
  • Suspend racing until conditions improve.
  • Cancel individual events or the entire event if participant safety cannot be reasonably assured.

 

Decision Authority:

Final decisions regarding weather-related operational changes rest solely with ViM Racing in consultation with local emergency services, public safety agencies, weather professionals, medical personnel, and other key stakeholders.

 

Communication:

Any weather-related changes will be communicated to participants, volunteers, staff, sponsors, and spectators as quickly as practical through available communication channels, including:

  • Email notifications
  • Text messaging (when available)
  • Social media platforms
  • Public address announcements
  • Volunteer and course marshal communications

 

Participants are responsible for monitoring official event communications before and during the event.

 

Participant Responsibility:

Participants should arrive prepared for changing weather conditions commonly experienced during cycling events. Riders are encouraged to carry appropriate clothing, hydration, nutrition, and equipment necessary to safely manage anticipated environmental conditions.

 

ViM Racing encourages participants to exercise sound judgment and discontinue participation if they believe continuing would place themselves or others at undue risk.

The Bootlegger is one of the most challenging and scenic gravel events of the year!
There are two route choices (58 and 85 miles) that both start and finish in downtown Lenoir, NC and travel through the beautiful and rugged Wilson Creek Gorge.

The 58 mile route has approximately 4500 feet of climbing while the 85 includes approximately 7250 feet of climbing.

Be sure to keep your head up and enjoy the scenery as the Bootlegger 100 takes you from historic downtown Lenoir and into the heart of the “other Pisgah,” also known as the Grandfather Ranger District.  Both the 85 and 58 mile options roll through the countryside before delivering you to a gravel wonderland with plenty of challenging terrain.  Just after you pass Coffey’s General Store and Museum, the two routes split, and the long course heads to the fabled Maple Sally Road.  

The course will be well marked in Pisgah Productions style and post-race meals and refreshments will be provided.

EventNotes:
Welcome to the Blackrocks Brewery Barry-Roubaix

Race Day: Saturday, April 17, 2027 
Presented by: Fox Subaru, Grand Rapids Chair Co., Grand Rapids Bicycle Co. 

OVERVIEW: 
We invite you to join us for the 18th edition of the Barry-Roubaix Killer Gravel Road Race. Like the spring classic it’s named after, Barry-Roubaix will test riders against rolling gravel roads, pavement, rough two track, rocks, sand, mud (and possibly snow and ice!) as you traverse the scenic roads of Barry County, Michigan.

We offer four race lengths to challenge riders of all abilities:
The 18-mile “Chiller” has approx. 1,200 feet of elevation.
The 36-mile “Thriller” climbs approx. 2,200 feet and offers the famous Sager Road two track.
The 62-mile “Killer” you can expect approx. 3,800 feet of elevation.
The 100-mile "Psycho-Killer" amasses approx. 7,000+ feet of elevation.

THE EVENT: 
Date:     Saturday, April 17, 2027 

Venue:  Start / Finish / Awards & After-Party takes
              place in downtown Hastings, Michigan 49058

Awards: Over $40,000 in cash and prizes (see our website for awards category details)

Details: Go to www.barry-roubaix.com for all the details of the event


2027 Registration Notes:
Our goal is to create fair and consistent competing race categories across distances and ages. Instead of selecting a predetermined distance age group, you’ll only need to select your race distance then Men, Women or Non-binary (unless you’re racing SS, Tandem, Fat Bike or Para-Athlete). We will create the final competing age group categories based on actual registration numbers, with a goal of keeping sizes reasonable yet competitive. Don't worry we'll have categories created and posted plenty early, so you have visibility into your race category competitors.

Race start waves, self-seeding:
In an effort to continue to improve course safety, rider interaction and overall race experience, we will once again let racers self-seed their start wave during the registration process.  Our goal is to create more consistency in start waves by having participants with similar speeds, competitiveness and anticipated pace going off in the same start wave. As part of the registration process, racers will “self-seed” themselves in the appropriate distance and race wave based on their expected finishing time. During the registration process, you’ll answer a question regarding which start wave and expected finishing time you anticipate. Once a start wave has reached our maximum quantity, you’ll need to select the next available wave (sign up early for your preferred wave). You will have the ability to change your own start wave selection, to another available start wave until the registration deadline on Friday 4/2/27 at 5pm ET. *If you change your original registered race distance, you’ll need go into your new race distance and select a new start wave based on your new race distance*

Race wave start times:
The 100-mile race will still start ay 7am. The 36-mile will go off at 9am followed by the 62-mile at 10am and finally the 18-mile at 10:15am. Given the timeframe we have to conduct the race this time sequence is the best solution to minimize interaction between the different race distances and riders of varying speeds on the intermingling courses.


Key Dates: 
Registration opens 11/14/26 at 9 AM ET.
Once the racer cap is met, open registration closes and the waitlist will open
Registration close 4/2/27 at 5PM ET. 
Distance changes, Race category changes and entry transfers…. close 4/2/27 at 5 PM ET. * No exceptions to this deadline

YOUTH (18 and under) 18-MILE & 36-Mile RACE FREE
Let’s continue to encourage the next generation to race and experience what we love about cycling and gravel. All youth 18 and under may register and race the 18 & 36-mile race distances for FREE - Courtesy of Grand Rapids Chair Co. 

Registration:
Please make sure your BikeReg account profile is up to date with the latest email address and contact information. We send all key race correspondence to the email you have listed on BikeReg!
NO Race license required.
NO Day of registration.
NO Deferrals

Category and distance changes: 
If your training didn't pan out as planned, you can change race distance or race category until the deadline on 4/3/26 at 5 PM EST.  There is a $10 charge for category changes. 

Waitlist Registration: 
Once the race is “sold out”, the wait list for all categories will open. You will be “in line” for the next registration transfer based on the date and time you registered for the wait list. The 18, 36, 62 and 100 mile categories roll up into one wait list. PLEASE NOTE THE WAIT LIST IS AUTOMATIC. YOU WILL BE CHARGED AND ENTERED INTO THE RACE IF YOU ARE NEXT ON THE LIST TO RECEIVE A TRANSFER. IF YOU END UP NOT WANTING AN ENTRY, REMOVE YOURSELF FROM THE LIST. 

Registration Transfers: 
Did your plans change, and you’ll no longer be able to attend the race? Don’t worry, you have until 4/2/27 to sell your entry to the next person on the wait list (as long as there is someone on the wait list) or find your own replacement racer and sell them your race entry. 
The race registration transfer process:
Sell your race entry to the next person on the waitlist; 
Once the race is Sold Out the wait list for all categories will open. Simply go into your race registration through your Bikereg account or registration confirmation email and select “withdraw entry”. If there is someone on the waitlist they will receive your entry and you'll receive a refund to your original payment method. * note - you won't see “withdraw entry” if there's nobody on the waitlist.
Sell your entry to someone you find: 
The original registered racer finds a person to sell their registration to and works out the selling price, payment arrangement and needs the buyers email address. The original registered racer then goes into their BikeReg race confirmation or account and selects “TRANSFER REGISTRATION”. Enter the email of the person buying your registration. The person transferring in gets an email, accepts the transfer, and goes to BikeReg and selects the category they will be racing in.  They will check out and pay the $10 transfer fee. 

**The event organizers reserve the right to delay, reschedule or cancel the race due to, but not limited to include; weather, emergencies and any unforeseen situations that may put at risk the safety of the racers, spectators, volunteers and general public.  No refunds or entry deferring will be provided, however the race organizers may offer registrants a partial refund or credit to a future race.

VISIT www.barry-roubaix.com for all the race details and rules

All races will follow a mass start format. Age-groups within each race will be dispatched in 2-minute increments.

PRIZES / PAYOUTS

The payout schedule for most MASS races can be found by clicking here MASS Cash Payouts. We have some pretty awesome medals for the other Cat 1-3s.

ENDURANCE - To be considered for the podium, cash prizes or awards in endurance, one must race for a minimum of 3 laps.

For all cash fields, a minimum of 6 starters to payout 3 deep, a minimum of 3 starters to payout first place. The race director reserves the right to not pay more than 50% of the field.

COURSE

Course .gpx file available under “downloads” and map available under “map.” Lap count and course subject to change.

WEATHER / RAIN DATE

Zip code 21921 for your weather app. This is a light rain or shine event. In the event of postponement, an announcement will appear on the MASS website by 6:00 pm the night before the race, unless we are able to make the call earlier. We will also contact all registered racers using the email address provided on your registration - make sure it's accurate.

The rain date is the following Saturday. All registrations will automatically carry over to the rain date. No action necessary on your part, 

If you can't make the rain date, consider buying refund insurance when you register (cannot be purchased retroactively).

REFUNDS / TRANSFERS 

The event has a NO REFUND POLICY. Make sure that you have no scheduling conflicts BEFORE you register. 

In the event of postponement or cancellation, registration fees will not be refunded by the event organizer unless you have purchased the $6 Refund Insurance with your entry fee. This optional purchase is offered under “EVENT ITEMS.” BikeReg platform fees and the insurance fee are not refunded.

NO INSURANCE = NO REFUND if we have to postpone or cancel the event. 

Refund Insurance is a smart purchase for those who know they CANNOT make the rain date.

You are allowed to TRANSFER your entry to someone else, before online registration closes, for the original transaction entry amount. You must coordinate with your replacement, who can choose any category in the event, and your replacement pays the difference in price of entry fee, if applicable. (No refund if they register for a lower cost entry, i.e. an adult transferring to a junior). And perhaps they’ll reimburse you for the original amount - that is to be worked out between you and them.

RULES

  • MASS Race Rules can be found HERE. This includes information regarding series rules, determining your racing age/category and upgrade policy.
  • MASS Rules apply to all races.
  • No e-bikes outside of the e-bike category.
  • Helmets must be worn at all times while riding, including warmups.
  • No earbuds permitted during pre-ride or races.
  • No course pre-riding during races.
  • Any rider littering the course with food packages or waste will be disqualified.
  • NO ALCOHOL is permitted within park property.

NO WATER PROVIDED - BRING YOUR OWN

You must provide your own water. Even if you are just doing one lap, you will need to HYDRATE so bring water with you.

FOOD VENDOR

TBA

PRE-RIDES

The park is open to the public. You may ride during open hours. We may or may not hold guided rides. If you are interested in leading a ride, please let us know. There will be no pre-riding or warming up on the course during any race. If found doing so, racers are subject to disqualification with no refund.

If pre-riding day-of, please be off the course by 8:45am on the day of the event.

NO CAMPING

There is no overnight camping. See here for Fair Hill Rules. The race directors are not campers. Please use the web to search, not our inbox.

KINDNESS IS KEY

Remember when you were a rookie? Let’s set a fabulous example for our junior racers and everyone else out there too! When overtaking a racer, be courteous. Communication is key! Announce yourself and pass only when you can safely do so; we want EVERYONE'S racing experience to be nothing short of positive! 

WATCH OUT FOR HORSES

Although we have a park permit, and we have signage up about our race, there may be other user groups in the park, including EQUESTRIAN TRAFFIC. Our course and roving marshals will be there to help deflect outside traffic and keep the course clear for you. However, if you do come across equestrian traffic, please be courteous and be a positive representation of mountain biking. We don't want to jeopardize future events. 

T-SHIRTS

Pre-order strongly encouraged because race-day inventory will be limited!

Premium, super soft, poly/cotton blend in both men's and women's cut. Graphic is also soft to the touch - none of that stiff plastisol ink! I’m a T shirt critic, so you know we spare no expense to bring you the best! Using the same style base T shirt (Next Level for men / Bella Canvas for women) as we did in the past for Firecracker and Granogue, sure to be one of your favorites.

Pre-ordered T-shirts can be picked up at the registration tent or purchased on-site. To ensure you get your preferred size, pre-ordering is strongly recommended.

PHOTOGRAPHY

Professional photography by First Place Photo. Link to photos to be emailed to you after the race. 

MUSIC

We've curated a killer compilation of songs to kick up the excitement and amp up your motivation! Carrying over the Classic Rock vibe from Granogue, these songs will boost your confidence and get your blood pumping with a variety of energizing vibes. Think of music as your secret weapon - let it fuel your motivation and go crush this race! Each track hits differently, and hopefully, you will be able to find some that inspire you as you both prepare to race and as you sprint to the finish line!

Spring in Iowa, cold, hot, windy, calm, sunny, rainy, and of course snow. No weather is off the table. Welcome to the Pella Roubaix. Modeled after the European spring classics housed over Northern Europe, this event is sure to challenge you physically as much as mentally. Although it does not boast the cobbles of the French countryside, it will take you through the rolling hillside of multiple counties in south central Iowa. This is a multi-surface venture of both gravel and county paved roads alternating back and forth throughout the ride.

The ride will have a mass start at Iowa Bike Co. in downtown Pella starting at 10 AM. There will be a neutral roll out of town. The Gran Fondo will consist of a 56 km loop and is much less competitive. The longer course will be roughly 110km. Both will end outside of Pella. This is a self-supported ride and you are responsible for you. There will be a checkpoint on course. Awards will be presented for top 3 in each category. Courses will be sent to registered riders prior to start as well as further details.

Pella Roubaix Spring Classic

10 AM - Pella Roubaix

The Mohican Trail Jamboree is a way for you the rider to help support the very people that maintain and create the trails at Mohican State Park. The funds raised with this event allow the club to purchase supplies, tools, signs, and other equipment to maintain the trail system. Our club is for riders, by riders. Feel free to join us! https://www.ridemohican.com/join

The actual Jamboree will have several aid stations available with snacks and water. The number of aid stations depends on the route you choose. There will be sag available and several bail out points as well. Pizza and refreshments will be available afterwards.

Mohican-Malabar Bike Club (MMBC) is a 501 (c) (3) non-profit, volunteer-led organization with more than 20 members who give their time and talent to trail work, advocacy programs, and events to promote the sport they love.

The Mohican mountain bike trail is maintained solely by MMBC. Sustainable mountain biking, trail maintenance, and knowledge of the sport are our top priorities. We work closely with the Ohio Department of Natural Resources to preserve the forest and fauna in the state park.

The Dansville Dangler is the first gravel endurance event of the SSIC Gravel Series in Steuben County. Think of it as an early spring kick in the ass! The course consists of primarily gravel/dirt/seasonal roads with paved connectors. Youll be on a 16 mile Dirt Time Trial! The course will be open and traffic will be on the roads, so please obey all traffic signs and rules of the road. There are some steep downhills and some challenging uphills. Be prepared to come to a complete stop for any traffic. You will be timed over a 15 mile course with 1600'. 

Please reach out with any questions you may have. Gravel bikes recommended. Mountain bikes are capable. NO ROAD BIKES.

FRANZ WEBER MEMORIAL RIDE

Sunday, April 18, 2027

In April 2025 we lost our Club President, a great public servant, friend, and anchor of our community. Franz served the Hawaii Cycling Club and the entire Big Island community selflessly, generously, transparently, energetically, and unconditionally. We hold Franz in our permanent memory for his high ethical conduct, unwavering dedication to helping others, positive attitude, and endless energy and availability, especially to those in greatest need. Franz embodied all the virtues of a dedicated champion for the community and as an enduring model of generosity and kindness.

Join the Big Island cycling community in honoring Franz for this annual recreational group ride following Franz's favorite route from the Kona Community Aquatic Center to the Queen's Shops at Waikoloa. Riders have the option of a 24.5-mile one way ride or 49-mile round trip. Hospitality Coffee and Refreshments will be available in the parking lot behind Bike Works Beach & Sports at the Waikoloa Queens Shops. This event is intended for cyclists of all abilities and age levels who enjoy a reasonable level of cycling fitness. Ride whatever bike you prefer.

Disclosure: This is a non-sanctioned event. Participation in this event is AT YOUR OWN RISK. You are responsible for your own safety. A properly secured helmet is required at all times while riding
 

All participants will be asked to sign a liability waiver before the ride

The RELIANCE Deep Woods Gravel Grinder is a full weekend of grassroots gravel grinding in the Cherokee National Forest east of Chattanooga, TN, April 23-25! 

THE RACES
RELIANCE offers two race routes on Saturday (70 miles/8100 ft of climbing and 46 miles/5600 ft of climbing) and one race route on Sunday (28 miles/3700 ft of climbing). All three race routes will have separate podiums for all categories.

THE RIDES
RELIANCE also offers a relaxed 13-mile shakeout ride on Friday, along with challenging recreational routes of 24 miles on Saturday and 26 miles on Sunday. All routes will be timed and all two-day finishers will receive a finisher medal!

Plus
Music, Prizes, Food, Beer & Camping!

What to Expect: 

  • Amazing Scenery
  • Grassroots Camaraderie
  • Good Food & Tasty Beer!

What NOT to Expect: 

  • Flat Roads
  • Easy Routes
  • Champagne Gravel

Saturday Routes:

  • 25 miles, 2900 feet of climbing, 70% gravel
  • 46 miles, 5600 feet of climbing, 50% gravel (race route)
  • 70 miles, 8100 feet of climbing, 60% gravel (race route)

Sunday Routes:

  • 26 miles, 2900 feet of climbing, 60% gravel
  • 28 miles, 3700 feet of climbing, 70% gravel (race route)

All routes will be timed, and Prizes & Awards will be presented to the top 3 in each race category both Saturday and Sunday.

All riders will have access to well stocked aid stations on the routes and will enjoy post-ride food, beer, live music and festivities both Saturday and Sunday after the rides! Free swag like water bottles, pint glasses, bandanas and koozies are included in the price, and we'll also have plenty of Tennessee Gravel merch available both days!

We are SOLD OUT of the reservable campsites at our homebase at Hiwassee Outfitters. However, free camping will be available nearby on a first-come first-served basis. For all of the available camping options, please see tennesseegravel.com/reliance-camping. 

Discounted registration is available for veterans through our friends at Operation WarriorFit!

The event benefits SORBA Chattanooga. To learn more about what SORBA does for the local off-road cycling community and to join the club, check out sorbachattanooga.org/getinvolved.

The Open Range Gravel Race is an ultra-endurance bicycle race through a remote and rugged area of the state.  Start time for the 200k race is 8am and there will be a 10 MPH pace cutoff.  The distance for the 200k will be between 125 - 132 miles. If you don't think you can maintain a 10 mph average, please feel free to sign up for the 100k+ or the 50ish.  The 100k+ starts at 8:30am.  The 50ish starts at 9am

Pratt Volunteer Fire Department will handle Drop Bag and rider extraction service. If you want a drop bag delivered and returned, sign up for their service.  Proceeds go to support the Pratt Volunteer Fire Department.   

Sun City and Medicine Lodge will be the checkpoints for the race.  Sun City is around 35 mile mark and Medicine Lodge will be around mile 80.  Checkpoints will have water and light snacks.  There is a drop bag service available (proceeds support Pratt Volunteer Fire) to riders. Bring your nutrition in a clearly marked bag or soft-sided cooler and we'll move it to the checkpoint(s).  Heavy duty slider zip bags with ducktape and name work great!  If racing in the 200k they will take 2 bags (one for Sun City, one for Medicine Lodge- they will not move the same bag from checkpoint to checkpoint). 

The 50ish will be close to 50k (31 miles) this year and still get riders on a loop of private ranch lands.  There is no checkpoint on this route. 

While we do allow transfers up to registration close, we do not allow refunds for race fee.  If you think you might need a refund, we suggest the race insurance provided through BikeReg.  Proceeds from Open Range go to local non-profit.

www.openrangegravel.com

Saturday, April 24, 2027 - 9:00 a.m. 

The 100 Kilometer (63 mi.); 65 Kilometer (40 mi.); and 35 Kilometer (22 mi.) course is pedaled over paved roads in this beautiful and scenic North Texas area. It is a fast and challenging course. Be prepared for some long and steep climbs up rolling hills and the exhilaration you'll experience coming down!

ENTRY FEES: All entries postmarked by April 19TH, 2027, will be $50 per rider. All entries postmarked after April 19TH, 2027, and those who register the day of the ride will be $60 per rider. Registration and packet pick up will be on Friday from 9am-6pm @ the Sacred Heart Community Center - 706 North Main Street. On Saturday packet pick-up & day of registration will be from 7am-8:30am at Heritage Hall at 1902 Weber Ranch Rd., Muenster, Texas.

Please join us for refreshments at the Finish Area located on the South East corner of Heritage Park!  Free admission into GermanFest held at Heritage, which includes 2 FREE cold beers from the Muenster Jaycees trailer! You may purchase an event t-shirt for $10 as an add on when you register.

PLEASE NOTE: All entry fees are nonrefundable, as this fundraiser is very important for assisting our Sacred Heart Catholic School Family. All proceeds raised go directly to the school to assist a variety of needs including building and maintenance, textbooks and athletic expenses. Your support is greatly appreciated!

PRE-REGISTRATION AND PACKET PICK-UP: Registration and packet pick up will be on Friday from 9am-6pm @ the Sacred Heart Community Center - 706 North Main Street. On Saturday packet pick-up & day of registration will be from 7am-8:30am at Heritage Hall at 1902 Weber Ranch Rd., Muenster, Texas.

RULES: By law, and for your safety and protection, you MUST abide by all traffic laws throughout the ride. For your safety, helmets are expected to be worn. All riders under 18 must be accompanied by an adult.

REST STOPS/SAG WAGONS: Rest stops will be placed approximately 10-15 miles apart. Water, fruit and other liquids will be available. Medical aid will be provided along the route and at the finish. In addition, the route passes through areas where food and drink may be purchased. If at any point, our medical personnel determines that you should not continue, you will be detained and/or returned to the start by a sag wagon.

MEDICAL FACILITIES: The Muenster Memorial Hospital and local doctors and nurses will be available to assist with any complications. Emergency ambulance service and qualified paramedics will also be available.

WEATHER: Weather in North Central Texas is variable. Usually, the temperature will average 72 degrees at mid-afternoon. Wind usually plays a role during this annual event. Riders are cautioned to "plan your ride" considering temperature, humidity, & wind and then be careful to "ride your plan".

RAIN OR SHINE: There will be a ride and there will be no refunds. Rally begins at 9 AM! 

All proceeds from this event will benefit education for Sacred Heart Catholic School.

You aren't going to want to miss the 4th annual Coal Country Roubaix!  This gravel/dirt road ride will test your ability. Each course is filled with challenging climbs, lots of gravel, some technical downhills, minimal pavement, potentially mud and who knows maybe even snow!  

For 2027, there are FOUR route options - 35 miler, 100k, 100 mile & 300 miler. ALL routes are roughly 75% gravel roads! And, lots & lots of elevation! If you're looking for a challenging course, this is your event! Oh & did we mention the routes are in REVERSE this year?! 

The 2027 routes will be posted soon!

About The Ride:

All routes are scenic tours through back country roads with excellent views! These roads are great for riding. Little traffic, little maintenance & lots of fun! You never know what to expect, it all depends on the weather! Could be dry & fast. Could’ve just be a total mud fest. Either way, you don’t want to miss it!

Cyclocross, Mountain, Single-Speed, Fixed gear, Fat bikes, E-bikes and tandem bicycles are welcomed & encouraged!

The Bryce River Foundation is named in memory of Bryce River Waldrop, who we lost May 31, 2023.  The Foundation exists to come alongside mental health professionals and organizations who are providing suicide prevention training and education as well as good mental health practices and advocacy to end the stigma of mental health care.  

River fostered a love of cycling and bike repair so hosting a bike ride seemed to make a lot of sense.  Cycling was a coping mechanism for his depression, and it served him well over the years.  Exercise has also been proven to be beneficial to your mental health.

All proceeds will benefit the Bryce River Foundation and our mission to reduce and prevent suicide.

The ride features three routes:  a 7-mile Family Ride, a 27-mile intermediate route, and a 50-mile advanced route.  The 50-mile route will have an option to be shortened if a cutoff time is not met (more details in registration).  There are also registration options for folks who wish to support the event but don't care to ride ("Please Don't Make Me Ride!").  

For the 2nd year in a row, we are adding a 3-mile ruck.

This event will also have things for the whole family including a pop-up vendor market, fun jumps, and more.  Please join us as we Ride Towards Tomorrow!

Dirty Kitten Gralley Cat MMXXVII

"Where Gravel Meets Adventure"

April 24, 2027 @ Locust Hill Farm & Preserve - Rapidan, VA

Presented by Dirty Kitten Productions

 

So...What’s a “Gralley Cat”? 

Gravel + Alleycat + Adventure 

An “alleycat” is an unsanctioned, informal, underground bike race that traditionally takes place in cities and urban areas where participants race from one checkpoint to the next in an effort to complete all challenges and/or hit as many locations as possible. Think: Adventure Scavenger Hunt!

The Dirty Kitten Gralley Cat (DKGC) is a “choose-your-own-adventure” alley-cat style bike/run event on the grounds of Locust Hill Farm & Preserve (LHFP) in Rapidan, VA. Instead of following a set course from start to finish, participants are able to select their own route as they make their way around the property, visiting multiple checkpoints along the way. Both competitive & recreational participants are welcome. 

Participants have the choice of doing either a “short course” (~20 miles) or “long course" (~40 miles) individually, in pairs, or as small teams (runners can do anywhere from 5-20 miles). All participants are given a map of the course during check-in the morning of the event on which the checkpoints, course boundaries, and key navigational points are clearly marked. After visiting all designated checkpoints, participants return to the start area where their scorecards are verified and finish times recorded. 

NOTE: There is not a GPS route or map available for this event. Participants receive a paper or digital map of the course the morning of the event (no, you can't get a course map sooner so don't ask!)

Why Gralley Cat?

  • We think it’s cool, unique, and sounds fun!
  • It’s a good way to have a competitive event without a traditional mass start
  • This format gives us a chance to showcase different areas of the farm.
  • There are roads on LHFP that don’t really work in a traditional race format: Nobody wants to be chugging along in a group only to slam on their brakes and pull a 180 for an out-and-back during a race.
  • It can be as competitive or non-competitive as you make it. Want to plot the most efficient route and ride your heart out to get the fastest time? That’s cool. Want to tour the property and just have fun? That’s awesome, too! 

Categories: Solo, Duo, Team, Juniors* 

  • Solo - 1 participant (all levels)
  • Duo - 2 participants (all levels)
  • Team - 3, 4, or 5 participants (all levels)
  • Junior - participants under the age of 18

*We have both ride & run options. Run participants "choose their own adventure" and can cover anywhere up to 20 miles if they wish. The run course will be an abbreviated version of the ride course with run-specific checkpoints.

Registration: Reg opens January 2027 - fees increase on Feb 15th and April 1st

NOTE: Duo & Team participants must enter additional member names at registration

  • NEW "Purrathlon" (short run + ride): starting at $70 PER PERSON
  • Long Purrito (~40 miles): starting at $60 PER PERSON
  • Short Purrito (~20 miles): starting at $50 PER PERSON
  • Run (5-20 miles): starting at $30 PER PERSON
  • Juniors $5-10 OFF registration

*Day-of registration will be available 8-11am on site. An additional $5 fee will be added. 

Refunds & Transfers: 

There are NO refunds for this event. Transfers are available upon request (once the event is sold out). If the event must be canceled due to health, safety, or severe weather conditions, participants will receive a BikeReg credit equal to the FULL amount of their registration fee (not including any service fees) along with additional charges for merchandise, food, etc to be used toward another Dirty Kitten Productions event.

Rules: Participants are expected to follow all event rules & guidelines stated below 

HELMETS REQUIRED! NO AEROBARS!! 

Participants are asked to arrive at least 30 minutes before their designated start time, check in with a staff member at registration (cabin), warm up only in designated areas (not on course), be prepared when called to the starting area (all duo and team members must be present), and check-out at the finish when their ride/run is complete.

The course will be marked at turns and intersections. Some sections of the property will be off-limits (and marked “Do Not Enter”) during the event. Participants are expected to carry their course map at all times and pay close attention to signage. Only registered participants, volunteers, and staff are allowed on the course.

RIDERS: Gravel, cyclocross, and mountain bikes are recommended (anything with 32mm tires and up). Road bikes are not suggested for this course. If you ask us, we will tell you not to bring your road bike.

Check-In/Out and Start/Finish Info: 

Participants are asked to arrive at least 30 min prior to their designated start time (waves times will be emailed), check-in with a staff member at registration (by the cabin), warm-up in designated areas (not on course), be prepared when called to the “staging area” at the start/finish, and sign-out with a staff member when finished.

We will have staggered start times (10-15 minutes) from 9:00am-12:00pm. Runners start at 9am. Long Purrito participants will start 9am-11am and Short Purrito participants will start 10am-12pm. The last start time will be at 12pm. Participants will be assigned specific time slots either individually or in small groups/teams with others based on requested time frame during registration (1-hour blocks). 

ALL team/group members must be present at check-in before proceeding to the start area. Participants may ride for as long as they wish but must be finished by the designated cut-off time (3pm).

Water, Aid Stations, Support: 

There is some access to water on-site, but it is limited so please plan on bringing your own water, food, and supplies for before, during, and after your ride. 

Temperatures can range in the area during the spring: it may be warm or cool (50-75 degrees), depending on the time of day . We will have water and some single-serving nutrition products available at the start/finish area and aid station checkpoints on course. 

Participants will be asked to carry whatever they need with them for the entire time they are on course (2-3 hours): water, nutrition, flat pack, map, cell phone, etc. There will be 5-10 checkpoints (depending on distance) on course along with at least one fully-staffed “aid station” if participants need assistance. Staff members and volunteers will have cell phones and radios, signs will clearly direct riders “Back to Start/Finish” if needed, and First Aid will be available at the start/finish area. In case of an emergency, dial 911 and alert a staff member or volunteer if possible. 

Food & Beverages: 

Water and single-serving nutrition items will be available at the start/finish area, as well as at one staffed aid station along the course at the top of the Kitten Crusher. Post-ride food (prepared box lunches) will be available for participants at an additional charge (approx $20/each) during registration and must be pre-ordered in advance. Beverages will be provided at NO additional charge. Outside food and drinks are welcome (BYOB). Please be conscientious of your surroundings and use the trash cans/recycling bins that are provided or take your trash with you. We want to be invited back again.

Property Info: LHFP is a private, working farm. NO participants will be permitted on-site prior to the event. The property will open at 8:00am on Saturday, April 24, 2027

Nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Locust Hill Farm & Preserve (LHFP) encompasses over 5,000 continuous acres of privately owned land. 

You will explore LHFP on private, gravel & dirt, farm roads that run along the Robinson River, pass serene creeks and ponds, weave through open fields, and cross wooded forest trails. The area is truly an adventure cyclist’s dream as well as a beautiful wildlife haven.

What makes this event unique is that it is 100% unpaved on private property. However, LHFP is a working farm that we have so graciously received permission to use from the landowners for our events. Entering ANY private sections of the property before race day will be considered trespassing and could seriously jeopardize the event, as well as our ability to host anything at this venue in the future (and will result in immediate disqualification). This is why we are careful when publicly posting any of our course routes, maps, GPS files, and Strava links. 

NOTE: We know that Dirty Kitten GPS tracks and Strava segments have been made public, but please remember that this is private property and LHFP roads may not be accessed any time outside of an official event. We ask that participants respect our landowner’s requests and know that the Dirty Kitten Crew does everything possible to ensure rider safety and provide accurate, up-to-date information before each event. 

Course Info: DKGC is a “choose-your-own-adventure” gravel event spanning approximately 20-40 miles and anywhere from 1,000 to 2,000 or more ft of elevation gain (depending on distance and route). 

The course is 100% unpaved with mostly gravel roads and dirt trails: the majority of terrain is on private farm roads with some dirt and grass double-track sections. It varies from smooth, groomed roads to rough, choppy areas with the possibility of mud if there is rain.

Participants choose their own route according to a course map provided at the start of the event. The majority of the course is on private farm roads with one section that follows a quiet, local, gravel road (Robinson River Road/Rt.721). Riders are expected to stay right of center and obey regular traffic laws while runners should stay on the left side of the road when on the public road section. There will be course signs and markings along the route.

Keep in mind that this is a working farm. Although we are in constant contact with the landowners and farmers to ensure everyone’s safety, there is always a possibility that you will encounter farm vehicles, livestock, and wildlife during the event. Eyes up and ears open at all times!!

Navigation Info: You won’t need GPS to navigate. The nature of Gralley Cat is an adventure-expedition style event. 

Participants are given a map to navigate to different locations on the property depending on their chosen course/distance (long or short). The course map will be simple and the boundaries will be very clearly marked. The checkpoints will not be hidden and signs on the course will point you in their direction. We will give names to the roads on the farm and intersections will be clearly marked so you always know where you are. There will be markings that you can follow to get back to the start at any time. Participants are expected to carry or download the course map and pay close attention to signage. 

NOTE: There is not a GPS route or map available for this event. Participants receive a paper or digital map of the course the morning of the event (no, you can't get a course map sooner so don't ask!) 

Awards & Prizes: TBA - Provided by our amazing event partners and sponsors

There will be no awards ceremony or podiums. Scores & rankings will be posted during the week following the event and any prizes will be mailed to participants a few weeks later. Giveaways will be available at the event with donations going to local, non-profit organizations in the area (TBD). Recipients must be present to win. 

Facilities: Port-o-pots and wash stations will be available along with Medical/First-Aid if needed. 

Photography: Renowned Event Photographer, Bruce Buckley, will be on-site taking photos throughout the day that will be available on his website for purchase after the event. 

Directions: Check-in and Start/Finish @ Locust Hill Farm & Preserve - 8070 N James Madison Highway, Rapidan, VA 22733 (turn off Rt. 15/James Madison Highway and continue down the gravel road). Cell phone service is spotty and unreliable in this area so please plan ahead!

Parking: Grass/field parking. When you enter the farm, continue on the gravel road until you see volunteers and parking signs. The landowners have asked that we park in specific areas so as not to damage crops or interfere with livestock so please be patient and respect our signs/volunteers when you arrive. 

Accommodations: If you wish to stay the weekend, there are several nearby hotels and local AirBnB/B&B options in the area. The Baymont by Wyndham in Culpeper (formerly Best Western Culpeper Inn) has given us a group rate for the weekend ($99/night). Call and mention the event: Dirty Kitten Spring Ride (540-825-1253) to receive our special group rate. The discount is available through March. You may cancel up to 24 hours before arrival.

The basic tenants of the event to which all participants must adhere:

  1. Be fully self supported. Do not pre-stash or have others shuttle your food, water, tools or supplies while on the route. Plan accordingly.
  2. Know how to fix your stuff. No one will be sweeping the course. You need to be able to figure out your own extraction, if needed.
  3. Respect the course. Leave no trace ethos in place. Leave only tire tracks and footprints.
  4. Respect others. Other participants. Hikers. Equestrians. Forest Service.
  5. Like in years past, your participant number is the page you must grab at the check point from the book at that location. Wrong page or no page will equal "no check point".
  6. When on public and forst service roads, follow the rules of the road.
  7. Know how to navigate from point to point during the event. Never rely on others to be your naviagation.
  8. First aid and hydration are important. Prepare your own water and food or plan your food and water stops ahead of time.  

These races happen Rain or Shine, we do not cancel or postpone due to rain or snow.  These events can take you from sea level to over the 5k feet of elevation.  You may ride thru snow or cross streams and rivers so prepare yourself and keep an eye on the weather as event day approaches.  All registration sales are final
