War Daddy info (Scroll down for Sandlin's Shred)

War Daddy is a 65 mile mixed surface mountain bike race consisting of pristine pavement, glorious gravel, daunting dirt, and double track trails that will keep you begging for more.  Be ready to face some of the coolest areas in Kentucky including the infamous Hell for Certain, Devil's Jump, Twist N Sourwood, and the one and only War Daddy! The paved roads are awesome, the gravel roads will make you smile yet mad as hell, and the double track will make you tickled pink that you are near the end.  The race will be approximately 65 miles long with 3 to 4 aid stations, 2 of which will be drop bag locations.  The elevation of the route will be in the neighborhood of 7,000-8,000 ft. 

All categories will depart the Leslie County RV park at the same cruising pace as our neutral roll out leads you 5 miles into the town of Hyden.  The neutral is over as soon as you turn left onto Owlsnest Road and the race will promptly get spicy.  The roads will continue to be open to traffic and all laws of the road should be followed appropriately. We will have some voluteers pointing you in the right direction and slowing/stopping traffic in certain areas.  Also check out the Facebook page for our event which will be updated regularly with new info about the race as well as provide you with more information about the course.  As we ride the sections and get them dialed for race day we will be providing some updates of what to expect and what not to expect.

We will have a file before the event that you can download of the course.  We are going to work hard to have a very well marked course that you can race confidently knowing you are in the right place!   

We are still working out the details on how to incorporate all of the events that will be taking place before, during, and after the bike race, but rest assure you will get your belly full and be able to enjoy some good ol' bluegrass pickin and grinnin'! 

Of course  you will get a SICK T-shirt at packet pick up and the swag is usually pretty legit as well!

Sandlin's Shred

30 miles of awesome riding with 3,300 feet of elevation gain! Get warmed up on 2 miles of pavement before hitting the Red Bird Management Area and tackling an absolutely beautiful course that will take you up many rolling climbs. You'll also get to hammer up the infamous War Daddy climb while on your way to the only aid station which will be around mile 18.  Other than the 2 miles of pavement at the start, there is only one more short paved portion just before hitting the War Daddy climb. The rest of the race is all off road and very fun. The last 20 miles of this course is also the last 20 of the War Daddy race. This is really the best way to dip those toes in the game before diving head first into the full pull of War Daddy!

2026 Course Description:

Nestled in the Bavarian Alpine village of Helen, GA the ride starts in the heart of the North Georgia Mountains.  After rolling out of Helen the route hits the first timed segment at mile 2.5, where any riders with intentions of an overall podium finish will need to put their cards on the table from the start. The first time section immediately enters the mountainous area made famous by the 2003-2008 Tour de Georgia. In 2008, Unicoi Gap was the second to last climb on the approach to the race-deciding ascent up Brasstown Bald where Kanstantin Suitsou got the jump on Trent Lowe and Levi Leipheimer to win the event.  As riders tackle this timed section they cover over 7 miles and climb 1500ft to the top of Unicoi Gap. The climb is very gradual for several miles, before turning into a real alpine ascent. Enjoy the vistas of the Chattahoochee National Forest on the descent before turning left and climbing up and over Jack’s Gap.

A left turn on Richard Russell Scenic Hwy will put riders face to face with the 2nd timed section, Hogpen gap. Within 6.5 miles and another 1500ft, riders will reach the highest point on the course at 3469ft with ramps of 12%.  The views at the top of the surrounding peaks are breathtaking. Check your speed and be careful on the descent as there are many sharp turns. Enjoy the ride through the forest knowing that the hardest riding is behind you.

After tackling the two biggest climbs of the day riders will head east from Helen through Unicoi State Park. The route then hits the 3rd timed section at mile 46, comprised of rolling terrain for a 4 mile section. Riders then get to enjoy a non-timed section of the route for the next 30 miles as the route explore the area round Lake Burton and Seed Lake.  Be sure to save a bit of energy for the final time section, it only last just over 2 miles but at over 80 miles in to the day you'll need to find some go go power.

The route finishes back into the landmark town of Helen where, in 1969, local business owners collaborated to create what is now called “Bavaria in the Appalachians.” Just outside of Helen on the route is the Nacoochee Indian Mound, the center of the ancient Cherokee town of Gauxule, visited by Desoto in his search for gold.  Be sure to plan to stick around for beers, food and music served up at the finish line.

Welcome to Yachats, West Coast Gravel!

You’ve arrived at the “Gem of the Oregon Coast,” where towering Sitka spruces meet the crashing Pacific, and every sunset paints the sky in unforgettable hues.

This route is 20-30 minutes quicker than our Saturday event, with a remote start and finish 1 mile from Yachats! 

You're in for a special day!

Discover Your Coastal Playground

- Yachats State Recreation Area: Just steps from town, explore tide pools, picnic on seaside rocks, or simply listen to the surf roll in.

- Cape Perpetua: Drive a few miles south for panoramic ocean vistas, ancient forest trails like Amanda’s Trail, and Thor’s Well’s dramatic show of nature’s power.

- The Little Log Church & Museum: A charming historic venue perfect for a quiet moment of reflection—or even an impromptu photo op.

Savor Local Flavors

Fuel your adventures with fresh-caught seafood and local brews. Don’t miss Drift Inn or many other tempting places to dine  for a true taste of the coast.

Gather & Celebrate

Tonight, we’ll kick off at the Yachats Commons, the heart of community life—complete with ocean-inspired ambiance, local art, and excellent acoustics for our Graveo gathering.

We’re thrilled to host West Coast Gravel in our seaside hamlet. May your time here be filled with awe-inspiring landscapes, memorable connections, and the warm hospitality that makes Yachats so special. Welcome home to the Oregon Coast!

 

Mike and Andi Ripley and Crew

Full Hundo: This is the whole enchilada. Don't select this category without knowing that you are in for one hell of a challenge. This route is somewhere between 7,000 and 10,000 vertical feet of climbing (depending on the gps) and has broken many very experienced cyclists.

Please read the notes below:

Welcome to the Event Page for the Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo 2027. This is the 14th running of this event and we are so happy to have you back. Thanks for giving this a try or for coming back for another year. I hope you have a great ride, but before then, take a look at all of the notes below. All of the info you need is laid out on this page.

1. Registration: Registration will open to the public at 12:01am on July 16 for a limited time.  If you want to make it in, make sure you are in line. If the category you want is sold out, try another one or jump into the waitlist. Last year almost everyone who stayed on the waitlist made it into the ride.

2. Waitlist: If you registered for the waitlist, please do not contact and ask where you are on the list. If someone drops out, you will be added and you will get a confirmation from Bike Reg. If you change your plans and do not want to be on the waitlist, remove yourself. If you are next in line and a spot opens up, you will be moved into the category and charged the full amount for the position.

3. Transfer/Cancel: Bike reg changed how they handle transfers, so you can now do it on your own for a limited amount of time. To prevent too many people from grabbing spots they won't use, there is a $15 transfer fee if you change your mind about the ride. 

There is only one category for people who might want to cancel. If you are not in that category, you can not cancel your entry but you can transfer it to a friend. The "I want in, but might want out" category offers a bailout for those that have complicated schedules and might not be able to make it. You will be able to get most of your money back and someone else will be able to ride. That is pretty cool and way more than most rides offer. PLEASE SEE DETAILED CANCELATION INFO AT THE BOTTOM OF THIS SECTION. 

4. General: Please make sure you have the proper physical training, the proper type of bike, the proper mindset for a long hard day in the saddle, and some technical acumen to take care of yourself incase you have an equipment malfunction. This ride covers a vast geographic area so if you are in trouble, you might have to wait a while for someone to come bail you out.

This is a rain or shine event. There are no refunds for your entry due to poor weather. 

The promoter retains the right to remove any rider that behaves in an unsafe or undesirable manner at any time. No refunds will be issued for improper behavior.

5. Friends, Family,Fans, and Supporters: We love when friends and family come out to support riders. This ride was founded on some solid friendships and support from my family. We will never forget that, so we want your people to come join us as well. They just need to follow a few rules. 1. Don't block the roads if you follow along in a vehicle. 2. Drive safely around all riders. 3. Come to the after party, but buy a meal ticket if you want to eat. 4. Clean up after yourself.  

6: Volunteers: We need you! This ride does not happen without tons of volunteers so please come and join us in all of the fun. We feed you, put you in the raffle, get you a cool shirt, and give you a fun job that shouldn't take all day. If you volunteer, you could ride next year for free (non transferable)! We do have some volunteer jobs that will also allow you to reid. Get in touch for more info.

7: Charity: The Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo believes in giving back. One dollar of each entry is donated to the The Pennsylvania Interscholastic Cycling League. In addition, the ride makes a donation to the Keystone Youth Mountain Bike Team. You will see many of the students and their parents out volunteering on the event weekend. 

8: Merchandise: We will have the chance to buy different types of merchandise over the next few months. We always strive to bring you some awesome goodies and this year is no different. 

9: Lodging  We are working on a lodging sponsor 
There are also plenty of other places to stay in the region. A large group camps Frances Slocum state park each year. 

10. Starrucca Crossing  is a gravel ride in NEPA that shares some of the same roads as LLWH, but it takes you out a bit further than LLWH ever could. It is a bit smaller ride, but tons of fun. 

11. GJE?  George J. Engleman is my dad. He is a big reason why this ride even exists. He gave me the love of exploration and of riding my bike. He was my number one volunteer. He passed away in November of 2016. I and the ride miss him dearly. If you see his initials on some merch, know that he is/was a very special person.

Tim, My Dad, Charles, and Dave on LLWH1

What is  Your CANCELLATION POLICY? 

 

We begin planning, permitting, and purchasing items for an event well in advance based on your pre-registration. Therefore we have a strict no refund policy. Be aware when you decide to register. We feel like our flexible transfer and change policies should accommodate most people and situations.

  1. CVP CANCELLATION POLICY No refunds, No exceptions.
    1. 45 Days Prior to the event:  Deadline to Defer to the following year.  Deferrals are good for 1 year only. You can not defer a second year. You may transfer your entry to another person if you have a deferred entry, but it must be done 30 days prior to the event.
    2.  10 Days Prior to the Event;
      1. You may transfer your entry to a different participant using the online transfer tool. Registration is transferable to the current event and year only. The deadline to transfer is 10 days prior to the event online.
      2. You may cancel your entry and receive a credit valued at 30% of your entry fee to use toward any CVP event within 1 year of cancellation. You MUST cancel no less than 10 days prior to the scheduled event.
    3. 9-0 Days before the Event:  Cancellations less than 10 days prior to an event and no-shows do not qualify for a credit.
  2. Transfers and Changes 

YOU Can now edit items on your registration if you have a Bikereg Account.  Racer name, phone, address, and email. You can also change the team category or team names. 

Transfers and Category Changes must be made through your BikeReg Account. Some actions are not allowed if you register as a guest. Change fees will apply.

If you change to a lessor distance you will not receive a refund on the price difference but we will not charge you a change fee.

If you change to a higher-priced category you will pay the change fee + the price difference.

3. Participant Insurance 

We highly suggest you purchase the insurance with your registration provided by BikeReg. This is separate from our company and will cover you in case of illness,  injury, or event cancelations due to weather and other unforeseen situations.

If you purchase the insurance and have a claim, call BikeReg directly. We can not process your claim. But, if you file one it will void any rights to a credit or transfer on our end. You can’t do both.

EventNotes:
It's back for 2026! That's right, 2025 wasn't big enough to contain it and the Connecticut Segment Championship of the Universe (CSCU) is back for another 10ish weeks of joy.  

We all want to ride our bikes and could use a little friendly competition to beat the winter blues and maybe drop a few pounds.  We at STAGE 1 Cycling and AirLine Cycles have harnessed our collective brain power and stolen some good ideas from other smart people to bring you the Sixth Annual Connecticut Segment Championship of the Universe! How's it work? Simple...

THE BASICS

1. Starting January 4, 2026, we will announce a new Strava segment every other week over a 11 week period -- 5 segments total (giving us some room for weather adaptation). All segments will be within the state of Connecticut. Segments will vary from week to week - each one will be either road, gravel, or single track/mountain bike. BE READY FOR ANYTHING!
Use whichever bike you want, as long as it's not motorized. 

Segments this year will run from Monday to Sunday to be consistent with Strava's schedule.

Schedule: 

Segment 1: January 5 - January 18

Segment 2: January 19 - February 1

Segment 3: February 2 - February 15

Segment 4: February 16 - March 1

Segment 5: March 2 - March 15

Bonus week in the event of inclement weather: March 16 through 22

End of Challenge Party March 28, 2026

2. All competitors will have 2 weeks to ride the segment. Ride it as many times as you like.  We will count your fastest time. Once the 14-day period finishes, that segment is closed!

3. Each segment closes at the end of the day on Sunday.  All results must be posted publicly to Strava within 24-hours of the segment's Sunday closing.  Please make sure that no parts of your recorded segment are hidden.  Your segment must be appear on the Strava segment leaderboard to be included.

4. The top 3 overall winners in each category will be awarded prizes at the end of the series. The overall winner in each category will take home up to 50% of the registration fees we collect in their categories!    

5. Late Registration. Once a segment is completed and has been reported, it is final.  However, riders that learn about the series later may register for the CSCU after a segment(s) were already complete.  Late registrant results for any closed segments will not be included for the following reasons:  (1) Fairness - conditions change over time and the idea is that all competitors are doing the segment in the same two week window.  (2) Finality - if we reopen a segment for some people, we would have to reopen it for all.  (3) Results tracking - we can't keep updating overall results.  If you join late, you'll still have the chance to compete in all remaining individual segments, and we will still count all your points in the overall.  If you register late and miss any segments, you'll be at a disadvantage for an overall placement.  Have fun, this series is cheap and there's a free party at the end. 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS 

(definitely click this, you want these answers)

ADDITIONAL DETAILS:   

We're keeping registration pretty cheap, just $19.95.  Anyone may participate - no license is required!

You must use Strava to participate - it's the only way we can track results for this type of event. A couple of weeks before the first segment begins, we will invite you to join a Strava club that will enable us to communicate directly with you and allow you all to monitor the competition. Important - Your Strava data *should* also include either heartrate, cadence, or power data. Any one of those three are fine. We're not strict about this data, but it comes down to this: if we have to referee a dispute, we will rely on the available data, (i.e., HR/power/cadence to make our determination). If you only use the raw Strava data and nothing more, we won't be able to fully assess your dispute. Sorry, we just can't take your word for it. If you're a fast racer competing for a big prize, it's worth having the extra data. You can get a cadence sensor or heart rate strap pretty cheap and most can be linked via Bluetooth to a phone. 

All riders are responsible for their GPS data integrity. We have no relationship with Strava and are strictly using their platform as an easy means of tracking our participants. Same goes for Garmin, Wahoo, etc. In the event you have a data issue, you should contact Strava or your device manufacturer directly. Strava often can assist to recover or repair data. 

Prizes: We will award prizes to the top 3 overall riders in each category at the end of the CSCU series.  The overall winners will walk away with a check for 50% of all regular registration fees (not including the BikeReg administrative fee). If we get 50 riders in a category, that's about a $500 prize. AirLine Cycles and our other great sponsors have also kicked in swag.    

Scoring: Scoring rubric can be seen below and at this link.  There may be opportunities for bonus points, or time savings based on things like longest ride, hilliest ride, funniest costume, etc.  Expect bonuses to be worth 5 points or less.

Proceeds: (If there are any) will help support STAGE 1 Cycling's non-profit activities, including junior development, grassroots fun, trail maintenance and advocacy, and competitive events. Many thanks to all the riders who donated their winnings to Stage 1 junior programs last year! In the immortal words of Jack Nicholson, "You make me want to be a better man."

Things you should do:  Register and convince others to join the fun. The more people register, the more exciting the competition and the bigger the prizes. You should scout each segment before taking your best crack at it.  Then ride it a bunch more times to see if you can improve your time and because riding is fun! Please contact us if you detect a problem with the segment and we'll see what we can do to resolve it. Feel free to suggest any "must do" segments you think we ought to consider. Suggestions will be considered. In general, we're looking for variety, beauty, fun, safety, and uniqueness. We avoid high traffic (car/pedestrian/etc.) areas.       

Things you shouldn't do: Don't cheat! No e-bikes or motorcycles, no tandems, no hanging on to cars, or snorting pixie dust.  Don't cut corners or attempt to gain an unfair advantage. Drafting is a no-go on this one. Don't attempt to tinker with your data. Absolutely no modifications may be made to any of the segments -- you ride it as it lays. Be a straight shooter. Cheaters will be disqualified.

Things you also shouldn't do:  Don't get sick. Don't crash or do anything silly, dangerous, or illegal. Don't sandbag an easier category: if you're super fast and fit, throw in with the Open ("Misfits") or Women's Open ("Runaways") so others have a shot. Be good ambassadors of the sport. Don't hide your rides on Strava. Be kind to everyone you see. Buy lemonade from kids, donate to charities, frolic in meadows, and so forth. Please inspect the segment before riding and make good choices based on the conditions. Pretend your Nana is watching you -- even if it's from the grave! If we get a report of knuckled-headed chicanery, the consequences will be swift, severe, and brutal - see above.

Just to be 100% clear - you are in charge of you're own destiny.  You pick the bike, the time of your ride, your hair color, sock height, everything!  You are in complete control of your choices out there.  Yes, this is our way of both empowering you and completely DISCLAIMING ANY AND ALL LIABILITY! See? Isn't it wonderfully liberating? Have fun and make good choices out there. :-) 

SOME COMMON QUESTIONS: 

Can I register in multiple categories?

Yes, you can register in every category in which you are eligible to compete. Your best ride on each segment will apply in each category you enter. 

What will the segments be like?  Segments will be either road, mountain bike, or gravel or a mixture of all three. You can pick whatever bike you want and you can stage different bikes along the route if you want. The selected segments will generally be a mile or longer and will be reasonably easy to navigate. We will think hard about the segments and try an pick sections that will be fun, interesting, and challenging.  

What if I don't live in CT?  Well, you should probably move here. Kidding, we don't take just anyone... (Also kidding, we do.) Anyone is welcome to come join the fun -- even New Yorkers! :P  Your drive may be a little longer, but it will be worth it. 

What if there's a tie?  In the event of a tie on an individual segment, the riders that tie will have the total number of points for those places added and then divided by the number of riders that tied. (i.e. if 2 riders tie and the points for those places are 10 and 9 points, each rider will receive 9.5 points towards the final tally). In the unlikely event of an overall tie, the winners will split the prize.  Riders will have the option to race for it at the party, but both parties must agree to this stipulation and are not allowed to complain about the outcome.

Can I swap categories?  Yes, until the conclusion of the first segment. We figured it's reasonable to give people through the end of the first round to figure out where they best fit.

Are you dropping the lowest time/score? No. We're offering two weeks to complete each segment.  We recognize that this is winter time and conditions could vary significantly.  That's why we're offering a 14 day window for riders to complete each segment. In the event that's not enough time due to weather conditions or some other force (e.g., legal quarantine) we reserve the right to cancel the segment for that week and either reschedule it at the end of the segment series or double it up with another week. 

GPS Drift - GPS Drift happens.  We will choose/create segments thoughtfully to try to avoid this.  If we find a particular segment has an issue near the start or the finish, we reserve the right to shorten or replace that segment to accurately capture the results of the challenge.

Can I complain about stuff?  Sure you can! Just remember that others may complain back.  Also, remember that this is an unsanctioned segment series. In the grand scheme of things, it's just not that important. If nothing else, everyone gets to attend the free party at the end. Go have have fun and don't sweat the petty stuff.

CSCU is an inclusive event that is safe and welcoming to all participants, regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, religion, disability, or ethnic origin. Athletes are allowed to compete in the gender category that they identify as. Non-Binary athletes are welcome to compete in any of the Men and Women categories. 

We strive to create an atmosphere that makes all feel welcome. From Pros to first-time racers, from staff to spectators, we will not accept behavior that is deemed to be bullying or any form of harassment and violators will be asked to leave.  

At any point, if you feel uncomfortable or unsafe or see behavior that seems to be making someone else uncomfortable, please speak to an official or staff member.

EventNotes:
The Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race (PMBAR) is the absolute pinnacle of MTB Adventure Racing. A mix of brutal and beautiful, this test of spirit and camaraderie tasks teams of two racers to reach 4 of 5 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish as fast as possible. The team with the lowest overall time wins. Checkpoint locations remain secret until start-time and there is no suggested route. Routes vary between 50-80 miles, include 9,000-15,000 feet of climbing, and take 7-14 hours to complete.

PMBAR is held deep in the Pisgah National Forest, one of the most beautiful, rugged, and unforgiving areas in the nation. There will be little to no water or food support on course. Once you leave the start/finish you are on your own. There will be no drops, sag wagons, or other outside support available. Be prepared for any circumstances you may encounter including, but not limited to: medical emergencies, navigational errors, inoperable equipment, wild animals, and stinging/poisonous insects and plants.

 

SCHEDULE OF EVENTS:

Friday 5PM-10PM – SIGN-IN OPEN 

Saturday 5:30AM-7:30AM -SIGN-IN OPEN 
Saturday 7:45AM – Mandatory Racer Meeting
Saturday 8AM – Race Start
Saturday 10PM – Race Final Cutoff

RULES:

1. Have Fun!
2. READ and UNDERSTAND the RULES. Ignorance of the rules is no excuse.
3. Team members must stay together at all times.
4. Teams must have their bikes and all other required gear at all times.
5. Approved cycling helmets must be worn at all times while riding.
6. Checkpoints may be reached in ANY ORDER.
7. Teams must reach FOUR (4) out of FIVE (5) checkpoints TO FINISH.
8. Teams that reach FIVE (5) checkpoints will be awarded a TWO (2) HOUR time bonus.
9. There will be required gear checks on course. Teams will receive a TWO (2) HOUR time penalty for each piece of missing required gear.
10. The team with the LEAST OVERALL TIME (after bonuses and penalties) WINS!!!
11. USE of OFF-MAP and HIKING-ONLY trails is STRICTLY PROHIBITED.
      A. Racers are required to use the Pisgah Map Company – Pisgah District map.
      B. Racers may NOT use other online maps or applications (i.e. Trailforks).
13. NO BUSHWHACKING. Stay on approved trails and roads.
14. Electric Assist ('E') Bikes are prohibitted.
15. RACE CUTOFF TIME: 10:00PM
16. SIGN-IN and return your TIMING CHIP upon completion of the event. PLEASE, THIS INCLUDES DNF teams. 
17. The Race Director reserves the right to disqualify any team for any reason.

VENUE:

Sign-in and Start/Finish will be in the field directly across US276 from Davidson River Campground in Pisgah Forest, NC.

OTHER:

1. PLEASE DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE EXTREME DIFFICULTY OF THIS EVENT.
2. We have very limited parking. Please consider leaving your car someplace other than the start/finish. For example, there are a few very large lots at the intersection of NC276 and NC280. We will also be directing half of all vehicles that arrive to the Ranger Station. Please be prepared for that possibility. Please show up early.
3. All gravel roads used in the Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race will be OPEN to vehicle traffic. Please use common sense while on gravel roads. Stay to the right. Do not cut corners. Pass with care. Ride single file.
4. This event is under special use permit with the U.S. Forest Service.

note: DO NOT USE TRAILFORKS OR OTHER SOCIAL MAPS. USE OFFICIAL MAPS ONLY. Use of off-map trails will result in disqualification.

We recommend downloading the free Avenza Maps app and purchasing the Pisgah Map Company – Pisgah Ranger District map for the digital version of the official map.

SPONSORS:

Come and enjoy miles on miles of gravel roads around beautiful Wellsboro, Pennsylvania home of the PA Grand Canyon! We have another fresh course for 2027, a few roads overlap from previous years courses and we are changing the direction of travel on some favorite roads from years prior. This route, like every year, is a BEAST!

The Full MAMMOTH course is 136 miles and roughly 13,000 ft.+ of elevation gain to challenge even the most advanced riders. Those of you that choose to attempt the Full MAMMOTH will ride two separate non overlapping loops. Both loops begin and end at the same place in downtown Wellsboro. The morning loop is 71 miles in length and afternoon is 65 miles. Breakfast, lunch, dinner  and two aid stops are included with this option.

Half MAMMOTH riders will just ride the 71 mile morning loop along with the Full MAMMOTH riders but will be done riding after the morning loop. Breakfast, lunch and the morning aid stop are included with this option.

The Quarter MAMMOTH Route is an abbreviated version of what the Half MAMMOTH Route riders are doing. You still get breakfast and lunch as well as stopping at Aid 1 for espresso and baked goods but you only ride 29 miles and climb about 3000 ft. Not necessarily "beginner friendly" but still a challenge without absolutely destroying yourself.  Breakfast, lunch and the morning aid stop are included with this option.

All food choices are selected in the registration process. There will be Vegan options available at all meals and aid stations.

Roughly halfway through each loop there will be an absolute banger of an aid station. We work with local businesses to provide hearty food at aid stations, as well as the essentials. The morning aid stop is included with all registrations. The afternoon stop is included with only Full MAMMOTH Registrations.

Please keep in mind that there will be a support vehicle patrolling the course as well as sweep riders bringing up the rear but we highly recommend that you carry what you need for  roughly  35 mile stretches.

*THIS EVENT WILL HAPPEN RAIN OR SHINE.  We DO NOT offer refunds or deferrals as all the event food and promotional items are paid for and ordered ahead of time. PLEASE CONSIDER ADDING REG INSURANCE OFFERED THROUGH BIKEREG IF YOU ARE WORRIED ABOUT WEATHER ETC. AND GETTING REFUNDED.

*We try our best to mark this monster route but the weather the previous days to the event really can dictate how well it is marked. The safest option is to use a bicycle computer with navigation or a phone app like Komoot or RWGPS for navigation. A GPX file will be sent to the email you use to register a few weeks prior to the event.

All event day check in, meals, and after ride hang out will all be centralized around the Patterson Trailhead building.

Free parking is available at this venue. If you stay at the Hotels located in downtown Wellsboro you will only be about a 2 minute bicycle ride from the Start/Mid/Finish and riding down would leave more spots available for those that drove in, this is not a requirement just a suggestion.

If you have any additional questions please feel free to email us or PM us on Facebook or Instagram also keep an eye out on mammothendurancegravel.com for resources and information.

EventNotes:
Eleventh Annual Black Fork Gravel Grinder 

Presented by: Lauf

Saturday, May 1, 2027 @ 10:00am

Loudonville, Ohio

Welcome to the Black Fork!  This early season gravel road race and ride will test your spirit, legs, and lungs and is perfect for Mountain Bikers, Cyclocross Racers, Adventure Cyclists and Gravel Junkies itching for a challenge. The three route options near Loudonville, Ohio are almost entirely on gravel roads and have varying degrees of climbing.   The Ride (23 mile route) has just three big climbs, lots of rollers and great views for participants who may be new to gravel or don't have the legs and lungs to tackle the longer, more challenging distances.  The Original (30 mile route) has seven long, steep climbs that will test your strength, fast and furious downhills that will make you pucker, and an occasional smooth roller that will put a smile on your face.  And the Race (53 mile route) is for the advanced adventure junkie who just can't get enough gravel.  It has 10 big climbs that will test the strongest racers.  Regardless of which route you choose, none are easy so you'll definitely have earned your beer at the finish!

Go to blackforkgravelgrinder.com for all the event details.

Don’t miss out on Ohio's premier gravel event!

EventNotes:
Sixteenth Annual Belgian Waffle Ride California

 

May 1–2, 2027 | San Diego County, California

Hell of the North County

Welkom to the sixteenth annual Belgian Waffle Ride California. The one that started it all returns May 1–2, 2027, for another weekend of bikes, beautiful bad judgment and the kind of post-ride storytelling that gets better with every Belgian ale.

The Hell of the North (County) has always been built around Unroad: a course that refuses to settle on one surface or let riders settle into one rhythm. Pavement gives way to dirt, sand and rocky sectors. Climbs interrupt conversations. Technical terrain asks questions your training plan may have neglected.

Waffle, Wafer and Wanna offer three ways into the experience, bringing accomplished racers and everyday riders together over the same North County terrain. The festival gives friends, families and cycling partners a place to gather before the ride and stay long after it. Venue and weekend programming will be announced as they are finalized.

Weekend experience

The weekend brings together rider check-in, the Unroad Expo, riding and the post-ride gathering. Meet the brands, catch up with your people, eat waffles and leave enough time for the stories afterward. The detailed 2027 program, venue and start times will be announced on the event page.

2026 Course Reference

 

Figures reflect the 2026 Race Bijbel course numbers. Final 2027 routes, sector counts, feed zones and festival location will be confirmed separately.

Roadie Oh 

The 2027 Gran Roadie-Oh offers a 100-mile Century with 6,172 feet of climbing, a Metric Century with over 4,000 feet, and a 50-km-mile short ride with 1,500 of climbing. Details of the 2027 Roadie-Oh and Dubbel Header will be announced separately.

Series status

The 2027 Quad-Tripel Crown calendar and competition format are still being finalized. Participating events, scoring and the number of results required will be announced separately. Utah will not be part of the Crown series because it will operate as a standalone UCI Gravel World Series qualifier.

Sixteenth Annual BWR California Rider Information

Rider perks

The BWR rider offering includes the following. Final category details and partner offers will appear in registration and the Race Bijbel.

  • BWR musette bag from Neversecond with race-day essentials and sponsor swag

  • BWR branded memento or BWR Bucks for use with participating partners

  • Race number and RFID timing tag for the official finishing time

  • Pre- and post-ride waffles, coffee and beverages

  • Stocked feed zones with hydration and nutrition, including Neversecond

  • Marked courses, traffic control at designated locations and on-course support

  • Post-ride beer and the BWR community celebration

  • Finisher’s trophy beer, with the offering determined by distance and event

  • Unroad Expo access and opportunities to meet cycling brands and partners

  • Bragging rights and more than enough material for the next group ride

  • Podium recognition for the top three in each Waffle and Wafer age category and the top five overall, subject to final 2027 category rules

Official BWR t-shirts, apparel and branded gear will be available through registration and the BWR merchandise area at the expo.

BWR sponsors

We are grateful to the partners who help bring the Unroad to life: Neversecond, Capriroso, ALMSTHRE, The Lost Abbey, Athletic Brewing Co., Van Rysel Bikes, Unwaffle, UNDERBUDR, FORMULA 100, Bolt and Birdworx.

Build your fueling plan before race day with Neversecond. Partner products and any event offers will be shared through the official BWR channels.

The Dirty Bloom 50, presented by Nick McLean Real Estate Group, is the premier XC mountain bike and trail running event of Wenatchee's Apple Blossom Weekend!  This event is a fundraiser for Evergreen Mountain Bike Association and in partnership with the Chelan Douglas Land Trust. 

We're bringing some exciting changes this year, including new trails, improved routes, and more incredible singletrack than ever before! Get ready for an unforgettable adventure through some of North Central Washington's most scenic and challenging terrain.

We're also thrilled to announce that the Dirty Bloom 50 is now part of the National Ultra Endurance (NUE) Marathon Series! With 20 years of history, the NUE Series brings together some of the country's most exciting and challenging endurance mountain bike races.

Whether you're chasing NUE Series points, pushing your personal limits, or simply looking to experience some of the Pacific Northwest's best trails, the Dirty Bloom 50 promises an unforgettable combination of suffering, adventure, breathtaking scenery, and pure mountain bike stoke!

EventName: Gravel Roll - Veloboros at Phinizy Swamp
EventNotes:
The Ouroboros is an ancient Greek symbol of a serpent eating its own tail. It is a symbol of the endless cycle of renewal. As you know, the Gravel Roll is always looking for new things, new places, new adventures and, most of all, new fun.
 

Welcome to Veloboros at Phinizy Swamp, a brand-new gravel cycling experience coming to Augusta, Georgia on May 1, 2027.
What better place to experience the endless cycle than in an honest-to-goodness swamp? There are alligators, wildlife, and plenty of questionable decisions to be made.


We’re not going to hold you to traditional race distances. Instead, you can see how many laps of the swamp you can complete.
Choose your adventure: each one with a little more…souciant of the Snake Eating Its Tail.
 

3-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Short Course
5-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Intermediate Course
7-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Long Course

Each lap is about 6.5 miles of 100% unpaved, traffic-free riding through Phinizy Swamp.

Ride as many laps as you can as a solo rider or put together a team of up to six riders to complete as many laps as possible in a relay fashion.
Whether you are trying to win the race or just trying to finish the event, there is a place for you in the swamp.
Every Lap Leads Back to the Party.


At the heart of Veloboros is our central Party Village, where every lap begins and ends. The FOUR Fs of your friends, family, food, and festivities are never more than one lap away. So complete another loop, grab some food, socialize with your crew, or take a break before heading back out on the course. Or, just put your head down and grind away on your stem. We don’t care how you complete the event, as long as you are having fun. And, if you make a wrong turn, don’t worry about getting lost, because you can get a ride behind Uncle Orville’s airboat back on course!
 

You decide how seriously to take the challenge. We're just here to make sure you have a good time.

We have some swampy shenanigans in store as well.


Phinizy Swamp is home to an incredible collection of birds, alligators, and other wildlife, and we're incorporating that natural wonder into the experience with a swamp-themed scavenger hunt and other surprises throughout the day.

Keep your eyes open. You never know what you'll spot between laps.


Our goal for the day is a great day of bikes, friends, nature and fun. You can come to race, you can come to ride, or you can come to hang out with friends.
This being the very first year we are going to limit registration to 150 riders for year one. We want to make sure how many folks we can really have a good time with in the swamp.


The Details
Saturday, May 1, 2027
Phinizy Swamp | Augusta, Georgia
3-, 5-, and 7-hour challenges | Solo or teams of up to six
Approximately 6.5-mile loop | 100% unpaved | Closed to motor vehicle traffic

So gather your crew, circle the date, and prepare to go around in circles for a very good reason.

Course and Format Overview:

  • Total Distance: 240 miles across 12 laps of 20 miles

  • Lap Cutoff: Every lap starts precisely every 120 minutes

  • First Bell: Saturday, May 1, 2027 at 10:00 AM sharp

  • Profile: Rolling ridges, fast gravel, and stretches of valley pavement with roughly 950 feet of climbing per lap

  • Venue: Pea Ridge Bike Camp, 10542 Blue Jay Road, Pea Ridge, Arkansas 72751

Staging and Pit Setup: Every registered Reckonneur receives space for one 10x10 pop up tent inside the rider pit area to manage gear, hydration, and nutrition during the event. Dedicated pit space is included with your entry.

Camping and Rig Parking: If you plan to arrive on Friday, stay through Sunday, or require space for an RV, vehicle rig, or pit crew encampment, you must book an official campsite in advance through Hipcamp. Space at Pea Ridge Bike Camp is limited, so reserve early if you need overnight accommodations.

Category Details (For the Single Reckonneur Entry):

  • Category Name: The Reckonneur

  • Distance: 240 Miles (12 Laps)

  • Description: The solitary entry category for all starters. Toe the line, manage the clock, and survive the toll.

Event Rules and Rider Requirements:

This is a true grassroots, do it yourself adventure challenge. No roads are closed for this event, and all participants must obey standard rules of the road at all times. Expect open rural traffic, county intersections, and working farmland along the route. Every rider must be fully self reliant on course.

There are no relay teams, no tag teaming, and no split entries. Every Reckonneur registers, rides, and faces the clock as an individual. You must complete every lap under your own power to remain in contention. Even the race organizer is toeing the line and riding the full event right alongside you.

Lighting and Night Riding: As the sun drops over the ridges, darkness sets in quickly on the rural backroads. Solid forward white lights and rear red blinkers are mandatory equipment for any lap undertaken between dusk and dawn. No light, no ride. 

Your front light must have sufficient output to navigate unlit gravel roads, potholes, and steep descents safely at speed. Rear lights must be visible from a significant distance to warn approaching motorists. Bring extra batteries, backup lights, or charging banks to keep your lighting operational throughout the entire night. Course marshals will pull any rider attempting to start a night lap without adequate illumination.

Enjoy the beauty of North Central Arkansas farmland. 

These routes are almost entirely gravel roads that roll past cow pastures and hay fields. 

Routes are surprisingly varied and engaging. Riders can expect scenic hilltops, open fields, and wooded creeks. 

Distance options are 100k and 50k. 

Please note that we measure distance in Arkansas with “ish"

Registration includes a custom tee shirt, custom finishers award, and post race meal.  

Meals for family/friends who are not racing are available during registration for an additional $15. If we are at risk of running out of food, we will not sell extra. 

Tee shirts for family/friends who are not racing are available during registration for an additional $20.

Shirt deadline to guarantee your shirt size is 4 weeks before registration cut-off. We typically announce the date on Facebook when it is close to deadline. If you register after cutoff, participants will still get a shirt, provided we have enough. Extras sold on race day once all participants receive their shirt.

Shirts are full color prints and we typically do a different color tee each year. 

We do not guarantee SWAG on race day registrations.

EventName: The 2027 Massochistah! (A Fundraiser For Youth and Adaptive Cycling)
EventNotes:
It's 2027, all over again!!!

 

 

Join Northampton Cycling Club for an exploration of the most scenic and challenging roads in western Massachusetts while supporting the expansion of cycling for all people in Hampshire and Franklin County.

 

 

ALL proceeds fund youth and adaptive cycling programs in Hampshire and Franklin County. We are completely volunteer-run to maximize support for these programs.

 

*253 years of tradition (give or take 249 years)

 

 

THE ETHOS

 

The Massochistah offers four distinct courses – each with its own character, all designed to challenge you. The longer courses were originally envisioned as spring warm-ups for Rasputitsa (RIP) and major gravel events. The shorter courses serve as an introduction to the great riding to be found in Western Massachusetts. 

 

While not a race, you will find PLENTY of motivation and maybe a few friendly rivalries along the way. In the past some very serious riders have used this as race prep for Rasputitsa, Unbound, Traka, etc.  The competitive spirit is alive and well here, particularly on the longer rides.  That said, this is not a race!  You will be riding on public roads and rights of way open to other users including walkers, cyclists, equestrians and motorized users.  Be aware of your surroundings at all times.  It is up to you to ensure crossing an intersection or a challenging section of trail is safe and within your abilities. 

 

Similarly, navigation is part of the challenge of these rides. If you are riding the MPC or Hurty, expect to receive a Ride with GPS route in the days before the event.  It is up to you to download the route (and the free app, if needed) to your smartphone, cycling computer or other device. We strongly recommend completing the download before traveling to the event.  The closer you get to the venue, the less reliable cell reception becomes. We will not have the resources to help you download the file and set up the app or your cycling computer when you arrive. You should have a strong working knowledge of the device you intend to use for navigation.  MPC and Hurty routes are not marked, so it is up to you to navigate the loop successfully!

If you are riding the Dirty or Flirty, the route will be marked. You will also be provided with a Ride with GPS file prior to the event and a cue sheet when you check-in.  Because route markings may move, disappear, or prove otherwise inaccurate, we strongly encourage Dirty and Flirty riders to track their own progress using a digital device or their cue sheet in addition to following route markers.  Navigating the short courses will be much less complicated than the long routes, but it is still possible to get lost!

 

You will experience a good bit of climbing, regardless of the route. The paved sections will be mostly low-traffic, although occasionally crossing or briefly following busier roadways is unavoidable.  The unpaved sections will range from smooth, recently-packed gravel to overgrown two-track jeep trails.  Some are maintained annually, but many are not.  You can expect to encounter surfaces such as loose rocks, tree roots, rock slabs, mud, slippery rocks and standing water, not to mention potholes and washboard.  We do our best to ensure routes are free of large logs or blow-downs, but cannot guarantee this.  Hills can be gentle or absurdly steep, but most are somewhere in-between.  Be ready to dismount your bike to get over an obstacle, up a hill, or through a slick situation.  Come prepared and willing to embrace the suck, even on the shorter rides.  Expect to get hungry, tired and dirty.

 

Of course, no suffering goes unrewarded!  Hot food, local beer, non-alcoholic beverages, and a full post-ride party are waiting for you back in Goshen!!

 

 

2027 ROUTES*

 

THE MARGARET PIWONKA CHALLENGE (aka MPC) — 8:00am Start

Course- TBD

The crown jewel. The beast. This is where reputations are made (mainly for crying).

Approximately 75 miles of jeep track, dirt roads, and pavement connectors. Some singletrack and hike-a-bike sections are possible. Plan on at least 120 ft/mi of elevation gain. If you don't know what that means, choose a different course.

 

What you need: A well-tuned bike with big tires (40mm+), big gears, and the skills and fitness to finish within 9 hours (approximate moving speed: 10mph). Most riders clock 5-7 hours on course.

The reality check: Due to the remote nature of portions of this route, be comfortable going 2.5-3 hours between fully stocked aid stations. If your bike breaks or you crash, it's a long walk—or longer wait—until help arrives. There will be time cutoffs at each of the two aid stations to ensure everyone gets a warm meal at the end.

The promise: An emailed, RWGPS route at least two days ahead of the event, two stocked aid stations and… an adventure. You'll love it. You’ll hate us. Then you’ll love us again when you get to the party at the finish line

 

THE HURTY — 9:00am Start

Course- TBD

The classic. Approximately 50 miles of quality dirt and pavement with brutal-but-doable climbs. Expect at least 100'/mi of elevation gain. This may not be the longest event, but it'll hurt just the same.

 

What you need: We recommend a gravel bike with well-functioning disc brakes and 35-45mm tires, though this route goes just fine on both road and gravel setups. The one you should choose depends on conditions and your comfort level on loose or washed-out descents. Most riders finish in 3.5-5 hours.

The promise: Stocked aid stations strategically placed 1.5-2 hours apart. At least one sag wagon on course for emergencies. A great ride and maybe some leg cramps to laugh about at the party. 

 

THE DIRTY — 10:00am Start

Course- TBD

The Dirty is a 25ish mile introduction, for those who want to flirt with hill town gravel without fear of major commitment; as our shortest option, it is also designed to be accessible for younger riders (accompanied by their adults).

 

What you need:  Just about any well-maintained bike with good gears and brakes.  Hybrid bikes, kids’ bikes, mountain bikes, road, gravel, CX should all work just great.  Just make sure you aren’t running some ultra-light tires that will deflate out of fear if they come within 5 feet of a rock – you gram-counters know who you are. It’s best to bring some snacks and a water bottle or two along with you to maintain energy and hydration.  During the ride the aid station always seem so very far away!

The promise: Both routes offer varied terrain with a little bit of everything. Expect to climb, but also to soak in beautiful spring scenery in western Massachusetts.  At least one stocked aid station and sag wagon support will be available.  Most riders finish in 2-3.5 hours.  IMPORTANT: Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult, regardless of route.

 *We have moved the event from Ashfield to Goshen – new location, but same great routes!

 

WEATHER & CONDITIONS

 

The Massochistah is an early-season event. In the hill towns, early season can mean many different weather conditions – sometimes all of them on the same day!

 

Come prepared for winter conditions, but pack sunscreen and electrolytes for heat. Expect roads in all types of shape: perfect, muddy, snow covered, flooded, bone dry…. welcome to spring in Western New England.  This ain’t Boston.   Plan accordingly. 

 

Organizers will communicate course updates and conditions the week of the event and reserve the right to shorten routes due to extremely foul weather or impassable sections. 

 

The event will only be cancelled if local or state authorities recommend it, or if Massachusetts declares a state of emergency in the area. This is just about the only condition when we will consider issuing refunds, or offer entry carry-over to next year.  Since this event is a fundraiser, no refunds will be made if you decide not to ride due to bad weather or weather-related course modifications.  Thanks for understanding!

RULES:

 1. Racers shall complete the entire event, and complete it on the same bicycle upon which the event was begun.

2. All repairs during the event shall be performed by the individual racer only. No outside help or assistance is permitted.

3. All spare parts and tools shall be carried by the individual racer (cannibalizing other bikes is not permitted).

4. Racers riding bikes have the right of way over racers walking bikes. BUT, YOU MUST WARN RACERS THAT YOU ARE APPROACHING THEM AND STATE WHICH SIDE YOU ARE ABOUT TO PASS THEM ON. When practical, bikers walking bikes should stay on the least redeemable section of the course, when being passed.

5. Short-cutting and/or cutting trail switchbacks shall result in disqualification.

6. Unsportsmanlike behavior and/or the use of profane language are grounds for warning, relegation, or disqualification. The penalty imposed shall be determined by the race director.

7. All local laws, rules and ordinances shall be observed during the participation in the Iron Furnace event.

8. Protests can be made by any registered participant of the Iron Furnace Race. The participant shall file the protest in writing with the Race Director or race official if the RD is not available. The protest period is immediately following the race and up to 15 minutes following the posting of the complete results for his/her class.

9. The Iron Furnace Race Director will make the final decision regarding any occurrence during the event.

10. No headphones or other devices that may prevent you from hearing cars, mt bikers, runners, etc. will be permitted while participating in this event.

 11. Bicycles used in competition must be propelled solely by the rider's legs, no electric bikes or peddle assist bicycles

What is Pedal Academy?

Pedal Academy is a fun, beginner-friendly cycling program for kids ages 4–9 that builds bike-handling skills, confidence, and a love of riding. Through age-appropriate drills, games, and group rides, kids learn cycling fundamentals while making friends and having fun on two wheels!

Tulane Cycling & Triathlon is a non-profit club sports program serving Tulane students, faculty, staff, alumni, and supporters in the New Orleans area. The club promotes all forms and levels of cycling and triathlon, with a keen focus on collegiate competition. Joining the club is easy! If you have any questions, don't hesitate to contact us.
